docs.title: agent-ops — restart resilience for agent work
docs.text: The machine/daemon restarts without warning and kills running workers. This system cannot stop that. It makes restarts survivable: workers checkpoint as they go, and after a restart the supervisor tells the parent agent exactly what died and how to re-spawn it.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File Purpose checkpoint.sh Worker checkpointing CLI (canonical tool) supervisor.sh Post-restart triage: flags stale/dead tasks, prints re-spawn briefs CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL.md The schema + rules workers follow RESUME_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md What a re-spawned worker must do, step by step IDEMPOTENCY.md How to write work so re-runs can't duplicate or corrupt it docs/MERGE-IT-YOURSELF-LAW.md Canonical owner law: merge clean green PRs yourself, never leave them for the owner checkpoints/ One JSON per task: <task_id>.json attic/ Deprecated alternate tooling (reference only)

docs.title: For the parent agent
docs.text:
Spawning a worker on a long task — include this in the brief:

Checkpoint your progress with ~/workspace/agent-ops/checkpoint.sh: init first with --goal and --resume-prompt, then beat every ~10 min and step after each unit of work. Read ~/workspace/agent-ops/IDEMPOTENCY.md and follow it.

After a restart — run the supervisor:

~/workspace/agent-ops/supervisor.sh            # stale threshold: 30 min
~/workspace/agent-ops/supervisor.sh --stale-minutes 10

It prints a ready-to-paste re-spawn brief per dead task. Paste each into a fresh subagent. The brief tells the worker to read its checkpoint and the resume template — not to redo completed steps.

docs.title: For workers
docs.text:
1. First action: checkpoint.sh init <task_id> --goal "..." --resume-prompt "...".
  2. Work in units. After each unit: checkpoint.sh step <task_id> "what you did".
  3. Long silent stretches: checkpoint.sh beat <task_id> every ~10 min.
  4. Decisions the next worker must honor: checkpoint.sh decide <task_id> "...".
  5. Blocked: checkpoint.sh block <task_id> "why". Unblocked: unblock.
  6. Done: checkpoint.sh status <task_id> completed.

Write outputs per IDEMPOTENCY.md (deterministic names, done-manifests, temp-then-move, no force-pushes).

docs.title: Honest limits
docs.text:
• Heartbeat staleness is a heuristic. A worker inside one long tool call can look stale while alive; a dead worker can look fresh if it beat right before dying. The supervisor reports; the parent agent decides.
  • Checkpoints live on this machine's disk. If the whole VM is wiped (not just restarted), checkpoints die with it — which is why important work also gets committed to its repo early and often.
  • A re-spawned worker must still verify checkpoint claims against reality (files exist? repo state matches?) before continuing. Trust, then verify.

docs.title: ANTI-CLOBBER LAWS (owner 2026-10-17 — the DXMMII 54k-file wipe)
docs.text:
On 2026-10-17, commit cd3bf38 ("DXMMII limb system", PR mhvnsnt/western-heart#221) deleted 54,456 files against 105 additions. The commit message said nothing about deletions. Nobody read the deletion list before merging. The repo was 99.996% gone. These laws exist so that never happens again. Every agent, every repo, every commit, every merge.

  1. DELETION CHECK — before every commit, read git status and the diff stat. Every deleted file in the diff must be something your task intended to delete. A deleted file your task did not delete on purpose means STOP: do not commit, do not push, report what you found. The working tree is wrong, not the task.

  2. OWN THE TREE — never git add -A or git commit -a in a working tree you did not fully populate yourself. Before committing, verify the tree is complete: file counts match the remote branch you branched from (your task's own additions and changes aside). A tree missing files you didn't delete is damaged — don't sweep it into history.

  3. CIRCUIT BREAKER — if a commit would delete more than a handful of files outside your task's scope, STOP and report instead of committing. A big deletion count is a hard stop, not a warning to scroll past. Committing unexplained deletions "and letting someone else figure it out" is the failure.

  4. SAY THE DELETIONS — the commit message names every deletion. One deleted file gets one line; many deleted files get a count plus what category went. A commit whose message and diff disagree is a hard failure — don't push it.

  5. MERGE GATE — the merger reads the PR's deletion list against the task description before merging. Unexplained deletions block the merge. "CI is green" does not excuse a deletion list the task never asked for. A red, conflicting, or lossy PR stays open with a comment naming the blocker.

(Co-authored with Aider and Copilot per the ALL-AGENTS-WORKFLOW LAW. Cline's seat stays open — its free-tier API was down during drafting.)

Instructions for every AI agent working in this repo.

docs.title: No-data-loss rules (MANDATORY)
docs.text: Read and follow docs/NO-DATA-LOSS-RULES.md (canonical: mhvnsnt/agent-ops). No force-push, no rebase/amend of pushed work, no history rewrite, no branch/asset deletion without backup + owner approval, PRs only, empty D-filter + gitleaks + green CI before merge, push incrementally, keep WORKLOG, back up and sha256-verify before disk cleanup, never touch other agents' or Muse's work.

docs.title: NO-SPARSE-COMMIT LAW (2026-10-23 — the cape-jones #219 main wipe)
docs.text: NEVER commit or push from a sparse/partial checkout. On 2026-10-23 the overnight pipeline committed PR #219 from a sparse checkout that materialized only docs/ — the merge DELETED the other 21 root entries from cape-jones main. A sparse checkout that looks complete can silently carry deletions. RULE: before any commit from a non-full clone, verify the working tree against the branch's real tree (diff the root listing, or compare tree SHAs). Default recovery path for a bad merge: revert the merge commit (-m 1) and re-add the branch's real payload — nothing lost on either side. When in doubt, build the commit via the Git Data API from verified tree SHAs instead of a local checkout. GOTCHA: gh's -f content=@file does NOT expand @file for the blobs API — base64 the content explicitly or the blob will contain the literal path string.

docs.title: MERGE QUEUE — COMING SOON (owner-ordered briefing, 2026-10-24)
docs.text:
Read this if you work on western-heart or agent-ops. Nothing changes today. This is advance notice only.

What is changing: soon, pull requests will merge one at a time, in a line, instead of every lane merging whenever it wants. Each PR in the line gets checked against the newest main before it goes in. That is called a merge queue.

Why: two lanes merged at almost the same time and one wiped out the other's work. The line stops that happening.

What changes for your lane, once the flip happens: - Merging a PR directly will stop working. GitHub will reject a direct merge. - Instead you add your PR to the queue. GitHub merges it when its turn comes, after re-checking it against the newest main. - If the queue asks you to update your branch (because main moved under you), update it and it goes back in line. Do not force-push. Do not merge main into your branch by hand to get around it. - The merge method stays "merge". Never squash, never rebase. Same as now.

When: NOT YET. The flip happens only after every active lane has confirmed it knows. This briefing is the advance notice — today, merging works exactly the way it always has.

How to confirm: reply "merge-queue briefing confirmed" in your chat, or drop that line as a comment on your PR, or tell the merge coordinator at your next check-in. Confirmations are tracked in mhvnsnt/agent-ops at MERGE-QUEUE-BRIEFING-CONFIRMATIONS-2026-10-24.md.

Status 2026-10-24: the queue plumbing is ready on both repos (western-heart PR #742 and agent-ops PR #39 both merged the merge_group triggers). The flip itself has NOT happened. No branch protection has changed.

docs.title: The incident
docs.text:
On 2026-10-17, commit cd3bf38 ("DXMMII limb system", branch feat/dxmmii-limb-system, merged via PR mhvnsnt/western-heart#221) deleted 54,456 files against 105 legitimate additions. The agent committed from a working tree that was missing tens of thousands of files; git add -A swept every missing file in as a deletion. The commit message said nothing about deletions. Nobody checked the deletion list before committing or merging.

The 105 additions were the agent's real work (all under tools/limb-system/dxmmii/). Everything deleted was recovered from git history — but it should never have happened.

How a tree gets gutted (any one of these is enough): - Working in a directory that isn't a complete clone (partial checkout, interrupted clone, or files removed to "save disk"). - A cleanup process, VM replacement, or another lane deleting files out from under the working tree. - The agent itself deleting directories it didn't think it needed.

In every case the failure is the same: git add -A turns "files missing from my tree" into "files deleted from the repo", silently.

docs.title: The law
docs.text:
1. Read your deletions before every commit. Run git status and git diff --cached --name-status. Every deleted file must be something your task meant to delete. If you see deletions you can't explain, STOP. Do not commit. Assume your environment is corrupted — do not try to "fix" it by committing.
  2. Never git add -A or git commit -a in a tree you didn't fully populate yourself. If you didn't clone it and watch it finish, verify the tree is complete first — compare file counts against the remote branch. A tree missing files turns every missing file into a deletion the second you stage everything.
  3. Say what you deleted, in the commit message. If you delete files, the message names the directories or file types and why. If the message says one thing and the diff shows 50,000 deletions, that's a hard failure — do not push it.
  4. Deletion circuit breaker. Any deletion outside your task's scope blocks the commit. "My task touches 10 files but the commit deletes 500" is never fine. Stop and report instead of committing.
  5. The merger checks the deletion list. Before merging any PR, read what it deletes and match it against the task. Deletions the task doesn't explain block the merge. A giant diff's deletions are never "probably fine."

docs.title: Co-authors
docs.text: Written with the full agent team per the owner's TEAM RELAY LAW and ALL-AGENTS-WORKFLOW LAW: Aider (rule 1 wording, the "assume your environment is corrupted" framing, and the hallucinated-deletion gap behind rule 3), Copilot (rule 1 name-status inspection, rule 4's clear stop condition). Cline was unresponsive at drafting time (its free-tier API hung); proceeded without it per the workflow law's exception clause.

docs.title: Propagation
docs.text: This law is appended to every mhvnsnt repo's AGENTS.md, each via branch → PR → merge per the MERGE-IT-YOURSELF LAW. This file is the canonical text; repo copies reference it.

docs.text:
Pre-reset backup of every git repo and work folder on the shared box. Nothing deleted; no main/default branch touched; no force-push.

Method: WIP snapshot = commit-tree from a temp index (working tree untouched, untracked included, .gitignore respected). Branch refs: backup/box-2026-10-14/<path-slug>/<branch>. gitleaks flagged findings (mostly vendored-code false positives like rcheevos aes.c) in every scanned range, so per the rule ALL ref backups went to private mhvnsnt/box-storage, not the origin repos. Pushes that box-storage rejected (index-pack fail on full history) were stored as incremental git bundles (restore: clone origin, then git fetch <bundle> 'refs/*:refs/*') on release box-backup-2026-10-14, size-verified.

docs.title: Checkpoint Protocol
docs.text:
How workers save progress so a machine/daemon restart doesn't destroy their work. Honest scope: this cannot prevent restarts. It makes every restart survivable: a re-spawned worker reads its checkpoint and continues instead of starting over.

Canonical tool: checkpoint.sh (in this directory). All commands below use it.

docs.title: When to checkpoint
docs.text:
Every worker on a multi-step task must:

  1. init a checkpoint as its first action, with --goal and --resume-prompt.
  2. beat at least every 10 minutes during long runs (cheap heartbeat).
  3. step after each completed unit of work (per card, per model, per batch item).
  4. next whenever the plan changes; decide for anything a future resume must honor.
  5. status completed when done; status failed/stalled with the reason when stuck.

If you only checkpoint at the end, you have no checkpoint.

docs.title: Schema
docs.text:
checkpoints/<task_id>.json:

Field Type Meaning task_id string Filename-safe id, e.g. judas-cards agent_id string|null Worker agent id (for tracing) repo string|null e.g. mhvnsnt/AshLanev2 branch string Working branch, default main goal string One-line: what the task is trying to achieve status enum running completed failed stalled spawned_at ISO-8601 UTC When the task started last_heartbeat ISO-8601 UTC Last beat/step/next/decide/status steps_completed [{at, step}] Done units. Do not redo these. next_steps [string] Where to continue key_paths [string] Files/dirs the work lives in decisions [{at, decision}] Binding unless the parent overrides blockers [{at, blocker}] What's stopping progress resume_prompt string|null The brief a re-spawned worker should follow

Writes are atomic (temp file + rename). A restart mid-write never leaves a half-written checkpoint.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
checkpoint.sh init TASK_ID --goal "..." [--repo R] [--branch B] [--agent-id ID] [--resume-prompt "..."]
checkpoint.sh beat TASK_ID
checkpoint.sh step TASK_ID "rendered judas-classic.webp"
checkpoint.sh next TASK_ID "render remaining 4 variants"
checkpoint.sh path TASK_ID "~/workspace/judas-cards/"
checkpoint.sh decide TASK_ID "keep all attires, never exclude versions"
checkpoint.sh block TASK_ID "waiting on Tripo export from owner"   # -> status=stalled
checkpoint.sh unblock TASK_ID                                       # -> status=running
checkpoint.sh status TASK_ID completed|failed|stalled|running
checkpoint.sh agent TASK_ID <agent-id>
checkpoint.sh show TASK_ID
checkpoint.sh list

docs.title: Reading someone else's checkpoint
docs.text: The supervisor (supervisor.sh) is tolerant of ad-hoc schemas — a worker that writes its own JSON by hand still gets flagged correctly. But workers SHOULD use checkpoint.sh: uniform schema means the re-spawn brief is complete (steps, next, paths, decisions, blockers).

docs.title: The resume contract
docs.text:
A re-spawned worker must read, in order: 1. checkpoints/<task_id>.json 2. RESUME_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md 3. IDEMPOTENCY.md

...then verify (does the repo/outputs match what the checkpoint claims?) before continuing. If the checkpoint is missing or unreadable: do not guess — report to the parent agent.

docs.title: END-OF-SESSION BACKUP (watchdog procedure)
docs.text: Run this when work is wrapping up, or when session/usage is ~90-95% spent (reserve enough budget: roughly 1 tool-minute per dirty clone plus upload time for large files). Follows docs/NO-DATA-LOSS-RULES.md.

docs.title: 1. Inventory every clone on the box
docs.text:
for g in $(find /workspace /home/box -name .git -maxdepth 6 -prune 2>/dev/null); do d=${g%/.git}
  dirty=$(git -C "$d" status --porcelain -uall | wc -l)
  unpushed=$(git -C "$d" log --oneline @{u}.. 2>/dev/null | wc -l || echo NOUPSTREAM)
  echo -e "$d\t$dirty\t$unpushed\t$(git -C "$d" branch --show-current)"; done
Target: every clone 0 dirty / 0 unpushed.

docs.title: 2. Push work to -wip branches (never main, never force)
docs.text:
git switch -c "$(git branch --show-current)-wip-$(date +%Y%m%d)"   # or keep the feature branch
git add -A && git commit -m "wip: end-of-session snapshot" && git push -u origin HEAD
Large binaries (> ~50 MB, or anything git refuses) go to Release assets instead — step 3.

docs.title: 3. Large files -> SHA-verified Release assets in mhvnsnt/box-storage
docs.text: scripts/bk.sh <clone-dir> <name> creates release box-2026-10-14-final-<name> (edit the tag prefix to today's date), uploads every dirty/untracked file, uploads a manifest (path, git status, sha256, asset name), then compares each release asset digest to the local sha256 and prints verified=N bad=M. bad must be 0.

docs.title: 4. Verify
docs.text:
• Branches: git ls-remote origin <branch> equals local git rev-parse HEAD; git ls-tree -r origin/<branch> contains the files.
  • Release assets: digest sha256:<x> equals local sha256sum.
  • Re-run the inventory: all 0/0.

docs.title: 5. Only then clean disk
docs.text:
• Delete only items that passed step 4. Log each removed path + where it is backed up + sha256 in WORKLOG / agent-ops/BOX-OFFLOAD-LOG.md.
  • Anything questionable: back it up again; do not delete.

docs.title: 6. Report
docs.text: Post per clone: dirty/unpushed counts, -wip branch names, release tags, verified/bad counts.

No connector/API credentials, no rclone/terabox CLI on the box (rclone has no official TeraBox backend). - GitHub (branches + SHA-verified box-storage Release assets) stays the PRIMARY, verified backup. TeraBox is SECONDARY only; never delete anything because it is "on TeraBox". - Upload is done through the browser by a desktop agent (one with a box desktop/browser), never by a headless/executor agent and never by signing in again — use the existing session only. - Procedure: (1) after steps 1-4, stage files in /workspace/terabox-out/<date>/ with the sha256 manifest from bk.sh; (2) desktop agent opens terabox.com in the box browser, uploads that folder to /box-backups/<date>/; (3) checks uploaded file count and sizes match the manifest; (4) logs folder path + counts in agent-ops/BOX-OFFLOAD-LOG.md. - Keep critical sets under the 30 GB permanent quota; anything above it may vanish when Premium+ lapses (~Oct 20, 2026).

docs.title: Problem 1 — GitHub release upload write-timeouts persisting for DAYS
docs.text:
Cost: longtail lane lost 1981.zip–1985.zip repeatedly Oct 20–22 ("FAILED after 4 retries (TimeoutError)" / "Connection aborted / write operation timed out"), one ~400MB whole-file upload at a time, no resume. Guardian offload verify-downloads also failing (FAIL download-back failed), blocking deletes while verify fails.

New finding (not in cluster 01): gh release upload's retry is exactly initial + 3 retries at a constant 200ms backoff, retrying only transport errors/5xx, with no low-speed stall detection (verified in cli/cli trunk pkg/cmd/release/shared/upload.go — the lane's "fails after 4 retries" symptom matches to the attempt). A stalled POST hangs indefinitely. gh also uses 5-way concurrency and --clobber deletes the old asset BEFORE re-uploading. Cluster 01's retry.py was wired into CloudDog only — and CloudDog's local copy was removed by owner order 2026-10-21, so standalone lanes have nothing.

Wired: lanes/resilient-gh-upload.sh + lanes/RESILIENT-GH-UPLOAD-SOP.md + lanes/tests/test-resilient-upload.sh (15/15 stubbed tests green): split-to-exactly-100MB parts (owner standard; RU_PART_SIZE is tests-only), sha256 manifest uploaded LAST (CloudDog-compatible schema), curl direct-POST to uploads.github.com with --speed-limit/--speed-time stall-kill (exit 28 → retry, never a multi-day hang), -T streaming, sequential parts, 8-attempt exponential backoff + jitter, retry only curl 7/28/52/55/56 + HTTP 5xx/429 (abort on 401/403/404/422), idempotent resume (size-matched parts skipped; mismatched parts DELETE-then-reuploaded — worst case re-sends 100MB), per-part size/digest verify + final asset-list check. Pattern adopted from ading2210/gh-large-releases — license verified LGPL-3.0, so the pattern (naming/manifest/delete-then-reupload) is adopted, code is NOT vendored. Stall-kill semantics from curl's documented --speed-limit (exit 28).

Recommendations (not wired): bring the longtail lane onto the 100MB split+manifest convention (its whole-file uploads are the other half of the failure); live-upload smoke test of the script against a scratch release (stubbed tests only so far — no repo artifacts created by this pass).

docs.title: Problem 2 — VM runtime restarts kill lanes AND their watchdogs
docs.text:
Cost: TTT2 pull lane died ~9 times in one night; its own watchdog went absent too; a coordinator died 8 min in with no checkpoint. Cluster 04 assumed the supervisor survives — it doesn't always.

New finding: this VM has no local cron daemon at all (no cron/crond binary, no /etc/crontab, no crond process — checked 2026-10-22), so @reboot crontab entries are not installable without apt/root. The runtime scheduler cron (which runs this task) DOES survive restarts — it is the only restart-resilient loop available. systemd user units already verified unavailable (cluster 04).

Wired (design only — NOT scheduled, NOT installed): lane-autostart/lane-autostart.sh + lanes.manifest + CRONTAB-TEMPLATE.txt + README-lane-autostart.md. flock(1) is the ONLY liveness authority (kernel releases locks on death/reboot — no stale-lock hazard, verified from sources); never kills live lanes; crash-loop guard (max restarts/hour → pause + state/<lane>.ESCALATE); watchdogs supervised too (own lock + heartbeat file — covers the dead-watchdog incident); setsid + env -i + explicit PATH launch discipline; all lanes ship DISABLED. Supervisor alternatives re-checked: supervisord (BSD-style) / circus (Apache-2.0) / honcho (MIT) / overmind (MIT) / s6 (ISC) — all SKIP (bootstrap gap without systemd, or no autorestart, or PID-1 rooting); no new evidence overturns cluster 04. Verified with my own eyes: bash -n clean, single-instance across 4 supervisor runs (1 real lane, "alive (lock held)" logs), crash-loop cap fired at max with ESCALATE written.

Blocked on OWNER APPROVAL (not installed): (1) creating the scheduler cron entry (~5 min) that runs lane-autostart.sh — the recommended wiring; (2) installing a local cron daemon if the @reboot supplement is ever wanted; (3) registering any actual lane (flipping no→yes in the manifest).

docs.title: Problem 3 — Merge-order hazards with the PR pile-up
docs.text:
Cost: western-heart PR #497 carried old geometry while PR #508's fix merged first — the #497 lane had to rebase preserving the fix; an in-flight A4 rig was built on pre-#508 geometry. Cluster 03 covered CI minutes/runners, not ordering.

Wired (no approval needed): merge-ops/pr-overlap.sh + merge-ops/PR-OVERLAP-README.md. Read-only gh calls: open PRs with file lists, pairwise overlap detection, mergeable/mergeStateStatus, suggested merge order. Live-tested against mhvnsnt/agent-ops: 17 open PRs listed, real overlaps flagged (CLAIMS.md shared by #9/#10/#11/#24, several already CONFLICTING). Makes the hazard visible; enforcement follows.

Verdicts: GitHub native merge queue — RECOMMEND as pilot ($0 for public org repos; true serialization via merge_group; merge method must be "merge" per owner law; needs branch protection + merge_group CI trigger). Kodiak — SKIP (license verified AGPL-3.0, and it doesn't serialize). bors-ng — SKIP (Apache-2.0, real serialization, setup tax too heavy for 135 repos). Mergify — CONDITIONAL power option (free for public repos, Depends-On cross-repo chains; only after a native pilot proves out). Merge-queue enablement needs OWNER APPROVAL (changes repo behavior).

docs.title: Problem 1 — Deploy blocked: 5,969 MB vs GitHub Pages 1 GB limit
docs.text:
Cost: live site https://mhvnsnt.github.io/western-heart/ frozen on the Oct 24 build; owner decision pending ("what gets cut").

Doc: research-friction-20261025/01-deploy-pages-limit.md.

Verified live (2026-10-25/26): Pages 1 GB published-site cap confirmed from GitHub's own docs (5,969 MB is 5.8× over — the full set can never ship on Pages). GitHub Release assets send NO CORS headers (curl-probed: 302 → release-assets.githubusercontent.com, 200, no Access-Control-Allow-Origin, signed URL ~1 h expiry) — direct in-game fetch() from Releases FAILS, so releases stay the store, not the runtime CDN. jsDelivr serves repo files ≤20 MB with CORS * + correct model/gltf-binary (live probe) and 403s an 86 MB GLB (documented 20 MB/file cap). Repo tree measured via the git-trees API: 176 GLBs >20 MB hold 5,914 MB (73% of GLB bytes); 98 GLBs >25 MiB (4,178 MB). Shell-only floor ≈ 70–170 MB (code ~10 MB + UI/portraits ~7.5 MB + 1 stage + 2 fighters + movesets/music). game/netlify.toml on main verified: publishes game/, proxies /roster/* etc. to Pages (so Netlify currently inherits the Pages problem).

Recommended (1st choice, $0): shell on Pages (~70–170 MB) + all GLBs on Cloudflare R2 free tier (whole set fits 10 GB, $0 egress, CORS-configurable). itch.io HTML5 shell + R2 lazy-load as the money path (shell fits the 500 MB / 1,000-file caps; HTML5 = donations only, selling needs a Downloadable build; payouts Direct to PayPal/Stripe or Collected, $5 min). jsDelivr as the small-file fast path (optional). Cloudflare Pages as shell-only host (unlimited bandwidth) or Netlify free as shell mirror (bandwidth figure uncertain under the 2025 credit system — verify at signup).

Excluded: full set on Pages, releases as runtime CDN, Cloudflare Pages full set (25 MiB/file cap on all plans), Vercel Hobby (non-commercial clause), git LFS / Actions artifacts (already excluded 2026-10-19).

Blocked: owner decision (split hosting vs cutting content — the recommendation makes cutting unnecessary); R2 signup (may ask for a payment method — owner-only per card rules); itch.io account + payout setup (owner phone-only).

docs.title: Problem 2 — Fight goes live +126s after stage confirm (play-verify run 18)
docs.text:
Cost: owner previously called the game unplayable; the 2-min load is part of that. 4 missing assets (404s) in the same run.

Doc: research-friction-20261025/02-load-time-126s.md.

Verified live (2026-10-26 ~04:09 UTC): deploy-manifest.json on the live site is summary-only (7,181 files / 5,647,298,304 B — no per-file list, no hashes), so no manifest check can run until build_pages.py emits a per-file manifest. HTTP Range works on Pages (live 206 + accept-ranges: bytes). Pages serves cache-control: max-age=600 — the browser HTTP cache only holds assets 10 minutes. three.js latest 0.186.1 (MIT); r186 release notes contain zero KTX2/GLTFLoader entries.

Recommended sequence (measure first, then cut): (1) own instrumentation in game/js/loadperf.js + ?loadreport FIRST — the 126s is unmeasured and no three.js load profiler exists to pull (stats-gl, MIT, is a dev-only frame overlay). (2) Kill the 404s: per-file asset-manifest.json from build_pages.py + ~100-line boot verifier (HEAD + size check, named failure, 3× retry); SRI does not apply to fetch()/GLB, and no lib exists for this. (3) If network-bound: KTX2/BasisU via existing gltfpack -tc (ETC1S color / UASTC normal, POT resize, own-eyes compare per fighter) + one shared KTX2Loader in game/js/assets.js; preload next fight during the current fight; Workbox SW + Cache Storage (Apache-2.0; its precache manifest doubles as the §4 verifier). (4) Draco: SKIP — meshopt already wired and decodes faster (1–3 GB/s SIMD). (5) Needle gltf-progressive (MIT): EVALUATE for stages only (17.4 MB → 715 KB first paint is real, but needs LOD-processed assets and buys nothing for fighters).

Correction (parent pass, 2026-10-25): the research doc's first draft said the 4 missing assets were "unnamed in the handoff" — wrong. They are named in the run-18 HTTP log (~/workspace/_playverify-20261025/http8123.log) and in memory: roster/demonio/anatomy/anatomy-layers.json, game-src/js/intro-interactions.js, customization/parts/no-mercy/glb/body_parts/model_1171.glb, customization/eye-library/eye-classic-original.png. game-src/js/... looks like a wrong-path bug (game-src/ vs game/js/) — a game-lane fix. Doc corrected before this PR.

Blocked: nothing above is proven to fix the 126s until the instrumentation runs. Do not start the KTX2 re-encode of all fighters before the measurement. Needle Cloud asset generation is a third-party service step (free tier: 30 optimizations) — owner call before any fighter GLB is uploaded to it.

docs.title: Fleet operating rules (overnight pipeline v2 — binding on every agent)
docs.text:
1. DONE MEANS VERIFIED ON MAIN. A piece of work is done only when its payload is confirmed present on its repo's main branch (contents API / git tree check), by the agent reporting it. A lane report, checkpoint status, heartbeat, or PR title is not proof. If you cannot verify it on main, it is not done — it belongs in the MERGE QUEUE with its real state. Never write "done", "merged", or "complete" for anything you did not verify on main yourself.
  2. QUEUE-FIRST. Finish before starting. Every work session works the MERGE QUEUE before any new intake: merge what's mergeable, fix what's fixable, PR what's branch-only, push what's local-only. New pulls/builds are last, and anything new enters the queue the same session until it is LANDED-VERIFIED.
  3. PROGRESS = ARTIFACTS, NOT HEARTBEATS. A checkpoint whose updated_at advances but which produced no new commits, files, or PR activity in 24h is STALLED, not running. Mark it stalled in the queue with what its core path is blocked on. (Failure this prevents: Tekken 6 decrypt6 sat "needs_owner" from 2026-10-16 with heartbeats flowing and zero core-path progress.)
  4. CONFLICTS KEEP BOTH SIDES. Resolving a merge conflict by dropping either side's work is a clobber — forbidden. Merge commits only; never rebase, squash, or force-push.
  5. BLOCKERS ARE CONCRETE DECISIONS. A blocker that needs the owner is stated as a specific question/decision, never a bare "needs owner" label. Items blocked >72h get flagged by name with their blocker.
  6. OWNER-HELD / DO-NOT-MERGE (never merge without the owner's explicit word): Bannon PR #78 (draft, excluded), western-heart PR #377 (stays open as evidence), cape-jones PRs #156/#157 (do-not-merge), cape-jones #167 + sitting-takes PRs (owner-held decision).
  7. REPO LAW: no repo is ever deleted; nothing gets deleted without the owner's explicit per-item sign-off. Orphan-history branches are archived, never deleted on an agent's own call.
  8. CANON RULE: game canon, notes, and development decisions are committed to the repos the day they are recorded. Assistant memory files are a working copy, never the only home. See HANDOFF-CANON.md.
  9. VERIFY-DONE SWEEP: past "done/merged" claims get re-verified against main on rotation; failures are reopened into the queue. The reopened false claims are listed at the bottom of MERGE-QUEUE.md.

docs.title: Picking up any workstream cold
docs.text:
1. Read this index, then the handoff doc for your workstream.
  2. Read your items in MERGE-QUEUE.md — that is your work list, in landing order.
  3. Verify current state yourself before acting: gh pr view, contents API, git log. Handoff docs are a map, not proof; the repos win any disagreement.
  4. Work branch → PR → merge (merge commit), then verify the payload on main and mark the queue item LANDED-VERIFIED with the merge sha.
  5. If you finish or stall, update the queue and the relevant handoff doc in the same PR. The next agent should never have to ask anyone where things stand.

docs.title: How Grok Bot works (copy this process)
docs.text:
Rules: money-machine-hq docs/AGENTS.md (laws 14 and 15 plus the adopted patterns), docs/muse-training-pack/ (PRE-FLIGHT.md, EXAMPLES.md), and the media-proof standard in AGENTS.md (also mirrored in Bannon AGENTS.md).

  1. Lock the method. Quote the owner's words verbatim. Name the method he said (e.g. "Smart Cut"). Say it back. If you can't do it that way, stop and say why. Never swap in a different method.
  2. Claim it. Add a line to CLAIMS.md (agent, task, branch, time).
  3. Branch plus PR, always. Never push to main. Fill every section of the PR template (instruction gate).
  4. Small pushes. Push each piece as soon as it's done. Don't sit on WIP.
  5. Edit in place. Open the existing file or project and change it. Never start a new copy.
  6. Never delete or overwrite his work without his explicit OK. Check the diff stat before every commit. Deletion guard: more than 20 files or anything in canon/ means stop and ask.
  7. Proof. Every "done" comes with evidence: renders/frames, checkerboard edge checks for cutouts (no rectangles), sha256 hashes of outputs, test or CI output, links.
  8. Honest status line first. Put "Failed", "Partial" or "Done" in the first line. Mock-tested is not live. Unreadable CI counts as a fail.
  9. Merge rule. Merge only if it merges cleanly, every check is verified green, and nothing is deleted. Otherwise leave it open and say why.
  10. Log the workflow. Record what you did, how, which tools and files, and where the output is, in the repo.
  11. Check before claiming done. Re-read his literal words and compare them to the result, method included.
  12. Hygiene. Run gitleaks before pushing. No secrets. Use unique temp file names.

docs.title: Common mistakes to avoid (added 2026-10-23, merge steward)
docs.text:
1. Pushing straight to main. It skips every guard. Example: the Megami expansion landed on western-heart main while its PR #793 was still open. Always go through branch + PR. See ANTI-CLOBBER-LAW.md.
  2. Merging red, or merging on a check you can't read. A 403, a cancelled run or a missing run counts as a FAIL. Verify through the Actions runs API.
  3. Resolving conflicts by picking one side. Never use "ours/theirs" on someone else's work. Append-only docs (WORKLOG.md, docs/owner-directives.md) get union-merged to keep both sides. Code conflicts go back to the author with a PR comment. See docs/NO-DATA-LOSS-RULES.md.
  4. Hand-tooling moves. Movement, crouch, jump, sidestep and every gap come from the TTT2/T6 teardowns (and the existing repos) until the owner says otherwise. Log the source file for each piece.
  5. Paraphrasing the method in the PR body. The instruction-gate needs "Method actually used" to match "Method the owner specified". Put the details under Proof, with paths in backticks.
  6. Stale gate on old PRs. The gate runs from the PR's own head. To pick up a gate fix, the author merges main into their branch. Don't force-push or rebase.
  7. Force-push, rebase, amend, reset --hard, or deleting branches. Never.
  8. Forgetting docs. Every change gets a WORKLOG entry and an update to HOW-TO-CONTINUE, so Muse and the owner can pick it up.

docs.title: Idempotency Rules — write work so a re-run can't duplicate or corrupt it
docs.text: Restart-resilience only works if resumed work doesn't trample itself. These rules are for every worker doing multi-step or batch work.

docs.title: 1. Outputs are keyed by input, not by run
docs.text:
• Name output files deterministically from their inputs (e.g. judas-classic.webp from JUDAS_classic.glb, never output-3.webp).
  • A re-run of the same step must produce the same filename. If the file already exists and is valid, skip the step.

docs.title: 2. Keep a done-manifest for batch work
docs.text:
For any loop over N items (cards, models, clips, files), maintain a manifest next to the outputs, e.g. ~/workspace/<task>/done.json:

{ "completed": ["judas-classic", "judas-painmaker"], "failed": [] }
  • Check the manifest before starting each item. Skip completed ones.
  • Append to the manifest AFTER the item's outputs are fully written and verified.
  • The manifest is the resume point. The checkpoint's steps_completed is the human-readable summary; the manifest is the machine truth.

docs.title: 3. Write temp, then move
docs.text:
• Never write directly over a final output path. Write to <output>.tmp-<pid> then os.replace() / mv into place.
  • A restart mid-write leaves a .tmp file, never a half-written final file.
  • On resume, delete stale *.tmp-* files before starting.

docs.title: 4. Git is a checkpoint too
docs.text:
• Commit working states on natural boundaries (per character, per batch). git log is a second resume source if the JSON checkpoint is lost.
  • Before pushing, check git log origin/<branch> --oneline -5 — if your commits are already there, don't push again.
  • Never git push --force from a resumed worker. If history diverged, stop and report.

docs.title: 5. Separate scratch per task
docs.text:
• Each task gets its own working directory: ~/workspace/<task-slug>/.
  • Never share scratch paths between tasks. Two workers writing to /tmp/x will corrupt each other after a restart reshuffles scheduling.
  • Ephemeral intermediates go in the task dir, not /tmp, unless they are truly disposable single-command artifacts.

docs.title: 6. Record-then-act for irreversible steps
docs.text:
For anything irreversible (push, publish, send, delete): 1. Verify the precondition (does the remote already have it?). 2. Do the action. 3. Record it in the checkpoint (step) AND the done-manifest immediately.

If the restart lands between 2 and 3, the resume verification in RESUME_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md step 3 catches it — which is why step 1 matters.

docs.title: 7. Heartbeats during long loops
docs.text:
• checkpoint.sh beat <TASK_ID> at least every 10 minutes.
  • In batch loops, beat (or record a step) after each item, not just at the end.
  • A 3-hour batch with one checkpoint at the end is the same as no checkpoint.

docs.title: 8. Decisions go in the checkpoint, not just chat
docs.text: Anything the parent/user decided mid-task ("keep all attires", "use X not Y") goes in checkpoint.sh decide. Chat history does not survive a restart; the checkpoint file does.

docs.title: Lane Guard — crash-resilient + collision-proof lanes
docs.text:
Two recurring failures (both happened on 2026-10-19):

  1. Daemon restarts kill lanes mid-work. A restart is a given. This is already survivable via checkpoint.sh + supervisor.sh (see CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL.md, RESUME_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md, IDEMPOTENCY.md). Nothing here replaces that protocol — lane-guard adds the missing pieces.
  2. Shared-checkout hazards. Multiple lanes working in ONE git checkout clobbered each other: a gap-audit lane committed onto another lane's branch; one lane's uncommitted work was stashed/restored by another.
  3. Cleanup lanes deleting live work. A cleanup lane deleted a 93%-complete Tekken 5 ISO download and trampled in-progress state.

docs.title: The toolkit (all in agent-ops, all additive)
docs.text:
Tool Solves lane-worktree.sh One git worktree + one branch per lane; a lanes registry; refuses cross-lane writes lane-ckpt.sh Thin wrapper over checkpoint.sh: begin, beat, step, plus resume (reads checkpoint, verifies key paths, prints the resume plan) guard-paths.sh Protected-paths registry + check / check-tree that every reaper (CloudDog, disk janitors, ad-hoc cleanup) must call before touching a path lanes.json Registry of active lanes (id, repo, worktree, branch, agent id, status) protected-paths.json Registry of protected paths (in-progress downloads, sacred manifests, active worktrees)

Registry state dir defaults to the agent-ops directory; override with LANE_GUARD_STATE_DIR (tests use a temp dir). Registry writes are atomic (tmp file + rename).

docs.title: The lane workflow (use it in every lane brief)
docs.text:
1. Spawn — get your own worktree. Never work inside another lane's dir, and never work directly in the primary checkout of a repo another lane might touch. 
    lane-worktree.sh spawn <lane-id> --repo <path-or-url> --branch lane/<lane-id>
    (Worktrees land in ~/workspace/agent-ops-worktrees/<lane-id> by default.)
  2. Checkpoint — first action in the lane, using lane-ckpt.sh begin (it is checkpoint.sh init): --goal and --resume-prompt are not optional. Then beat at least every ~10 min and step after every unit of work.
  3. Guard before writing — before writing into any directory you did not spawn, run: 
    lane-worktree.sh check <dir> --lane <lane-id>    # exit 1 = not yours, stop
    Or run commands inside your own worktree via lane-worktree.sh exec <lane-id> -- <cmd...>.
  4. Protect live state — downloading, extracting, uploading, or otherwise "in progress" files must be registered the moment the lane starts them: 
    guard-paths.sh add <file-or-dir> --kind download-in-progress --owner <lane-id>
    An active worktree is auto-registered on spawn and unregistered on release.
  5. Release — when the lane is done and its branch is pushed: lane-worktree.sh release <lane-id>. Release refuses to remove a worktree with uncommitted work; resolve manually, never with --force.
  6. After a restart — supervisor.sh tells the parent which lanes went stale. The re-spawned lane runs lane-ckpt.sh resume <task-id>: it reads the checkpoint, verifies each key path exists, lists steps already done (do NOT redo them) and the next steps. Missing checkpoint or missing paths → report to the parent, never guess. Full contract: RESUME_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md.

docs.title: Reaper contract (CloudDog and every cleanup lane)
docs.text:
Before deleting, quarantine-moving, or "tidying" ANY path, a reaper MUST run:

guard-paths.sh check-tree <path>     # exit 1 = PROTECTED: hands off, log, skip

Exit 1 prints the kind, the owning lane, and the note. There is no override flag, by design: the only way to free a protected path is for the owning lane to guard-paths.sh remove it (or finish and release its worktree).

docs.title: Research notes (2026-10-20, web search — durable execution literature)
docs.text:
Confirmed patterns, and where lane-guard implements them:

  • "An agent run is a job, not a request." Run id, named steps, checkpoint after every step, resume by name, idempotency key on every side effect. → checkpoint.sh already does this; lane-ckpt.sh resume is the resume-by-name entry point. (ekofyi.com, "Your AI Agent Is a Job, Not an HTTP Request", 2026-09-04)
  • Leases + heartbeats. A worker claims a job with a lease it renews via heartbeat; on lease expiry another worker reclaims and resumes from the checkpoint — at-least-once delivery makes idempotent steps mandatory. → Heartbeat = checkpoint.sh beat; staleness is measured by supervisor.sh. Lane-guard treats the CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL (beat every ~10 min, stale at 30 min) as the lease. No new lease system was invented. (dev.to, "long-running AI agents: Efficient Asynchronous Workflow Strategies"; dev.to, "Checkpoint Your Agent Jobs So Crashes Don't Mean Starting Over")
  • Durable execution (LangGraph-style). Checkpointer with a stable thread id; durability should be synchronous when a missed checkpoint means a duplicated side effect; assume steps re-execute on resume, so verify reality on every wake. → IDEMPOTENCY.md rules 1–3, 6 + lane-ckpt.sh resume's per-path verification. (vadim.blog, "Durable Execution in LangGraph")
  • Supervision layering. systemd Restart=on-failure + WatchdogSec (sd_notify) is the canonical native supervisor, with restart-burst limits so a crashing unit doesn't storm. On this VM, the Muse daemon restart is what kills lanes and the daemon is outside our control — so the surviving pattern is exactly: checkpoint (file state) + external watchdog (supervisor.sh) + re-spawn briefs. If a lane ever runs as a raw shell job under tmux, its tmux session must still drive lane-ckpt.sh beat; tmux alone preserves the terminal, not the work. (dev.to, "Self-Healing Services: systemd + Crontab + Watchdog Patterns")
  • One worktree per agent. The 2026 practitioner consensus for parallel coding agents: git worktree gives one branch + one directory per agent, physically preventing the branch-switch/stash collisions a shared checkout guarantees; integrate by merging branches, not by sharing files. Isolate only what mutates — readers may share a checkout, writers never. (dev.to: "Three AI Agents, One Laptop: The Git Worktree Trick...", "Running Coding Agents in Parallel with Git Worktrees", "A worktree per agent, so they never step on each other"; shipwithai.io, "Claude Code + Git Worktrees")

docs.title: What changed vs. the existing protocol
docs.text:
Nothing removed, nothing rewritten. CHECKPOINT_PROTOCOL.md, IDEMPOTENCY.md, checkpoint.sh, supervisor.sh stay byte-identical. Lane-guard adds only: per-lane worktree allocation + registry, a resume verifier on top of checkpoint.sh, and a protected-paths check reapers can call. Gaps it closes that the old protocol did not cover: worktree ownership (registry), cross-lane write refusal, and a callable "hands off this path" signal for cleanup tooling.

Related: FRICTION-RESEARCH-2026-10-19.md diagnosed the T5 ISO deletion mechanism (paused/resumable download older than 5 min slipped through CloudDog's is_inflight(); proposed fix: claims table + hard gates in reap paths). guard-paths.sh check-tree is the callable gate every reaper — CloudDog included — should call on every candidate path. A lane downloading anything big should also guard-paths.sh add <file> --kind download-in-progress so even a reaper without the claims table sees the protection.

docs.title: MERGE-IT-YOURSELF LAW (owner 2026-10-15) — canonical copy
docs.text:
"Stop leaving things open for me to merge... I don't like to manually handle PRs."

When a PR satisfies ALL merge conditions (GitHub says MERGEABLE, CI green, no-deletion guard clean, gitleaks clean, build passes), MERGE IT — do not leave it open for the owner. He does not want to manually handle PRs.

The merge must be CLEAN and NON-DESTRUCTIVE: merge commits, never rebase/squash/force-push; resolve conflicts by keeping both sides' work — nothing lost, nothing clobbered, nothing destroyed on either side. Verify the merged result still builds and passes tests before calling it done.

A PR that is red, conflicting, or would lose work stays OPEN with a comment naming the blocker (existing rule) — but the default for a clean, green PR is MERGE, never "leave it for the owner."

This REPLACES the old "open PR, do NOT merge (owner merges)" instruction everywhere it appears: worker briefs, coordinator instructions, handoff docs, repo AGENTS.md copies. Update them.

Carve-outs (standing owner decisions, not overridden): never merge a DRAFT PR; never merge a PR the owner explicitly excluded (e.g. Bannon #78 stays draft per owner 2026-10-15).

docs.title: NO-DATA-LOSS RULES (owner law — mhvnsnt)
docs.text: Canonical copy: mhvnsnt/agent-ops/docs/NO-DATA-LOSS-RULES.md. Every repo carries a copy at docs/NO-DATA-LOSS-RULES.md. These rules bind every agent (Grok Bot, Muse, Claude, Codex, Rocket, Dependabot owners, humans). They exist because work was lost before: history rewritten, files deleted or replaced, assets re-downloaded.

docs.title: 1. History is permanent
docs.text:
• NO git push --force / --force-with-lease / +refspec, on any branch that has ever been pushed.
  • NO git rebase, git commit --amend, git reset (soft/mixed/hard) or squash of commits that are already pushed.
  • NO git reset --hard, git checkout -- ., git clean -fd, git stash drop/clear on shared or someone else's work. Stash or commit to a -wip branch first.
  • NO git filter-repo, filter-branch, BFG, or any history rewrite.
  • NO branch or tag deletion (local-only scratch excepted) without explicit owner approval in chat. Merged PR branches are kept.
  • To undo: git revert (a new commit), never rewrite.

docs.title: 2. Assets are never lost
docs.text:
• NO deleting or replacing an asset (GLB/FBX/PNG/audio/video/zip/any binary) unless a backup exists first:
  • large binary → SHA-256-verified Release asset in mhvnsnt/box-storage (release digest must equal local sha256sum), or
  • a pushed backup/... / -wip branch containing the file, verified with git ls-tree.
  • Record the backup location + sha256 in WORKLOG before replacing.
  • Replacements are additive where possible (new filename/version), old file kept until owner approves removal.

docs.title: 3. Feature branches and PRs only
docs.text:
• Never push directly to main/default branch. Branch → PR → merge.
  • Merge origin/main INTO the feature branch to catch up (merge commit). Never rebase.
  • MERGE RULE — a PR merges only when ALL hold:
  • GitHub says MERGEABLE and mergeStateStatus CLEAN;
  • CI is confirmed green (every latest workflow run = success);
  • git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only origin/main...HEAD is EMPTY (or PR has owner label approved-deletion);
  • gitleaks detect is clean;
  • the build passes; nothing on main is broken.
  • Red or conflicting PRs stay OPEN with a comment naming the blocker. Never close someone else's PR.

docs.title: 4. Push incremental work as it gets done
docs.text:
• Commit and push small, often. Nothing valuable lives only on the box.
  • Before stopping: git status clean and git log @{u}.. empty in every clone (0 dirty / 0 unpushed). Use -wip branches for unfinished work.

docs.title: 5. WORKLOG
docs.text: • Every repo keeps WORKLOG.md. Log every change: date, agent, branch, what, why, source, backups made (with sha256).

docs.title: 6. Backup and verify before any disk cleanup
docs.text:
• Before deleting anything on disk: push it (branch or Release asset), then verify — git ls-remote / git ls-tree for code, release asset digest == sha256:<local sha256sum> for binaries.
  • Only verified items may be removed from disk. Anything in doubt is backed up again, never deleted.
  • See agent-ops/docs/END-OF-SESSION-BACKUP.md and agent-ops/scripts/bk.sh.

docs.title: 7. Never touch other agents' or Muse's work
docs.text: • Do not reset, rebase, overwrite, close, or delete another agent's branches, PRs, worktrees, stashes or files. Claim work in agent-ops/CLAIMS.md; coordinate, don't clobber.

docs.title: 8. Secrets
docs.text: • Never print or commit secrets (mask to 6 chars). gitleaks must be clean.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
• Branch ruleset on default branch: block force-push, block deletion, require PR (where plan allows).
  • CI workflow .github/workflows/no-deletion-guard.yml: fails any PR that deletes files unless labelled approved-deletion (owner-only label).

docs.title: Owner rules — 2026-10-23 (disk offload + merge rule) — Repo Co Dev
docs.text:
(a) Disk offload. Once local work is verified 100% pushed (0 dirty, 0 untracked, 0 stash, every local branch on the remote at the same or a later SHA, submodules included) or stored in box-storage, clear it off the box disk as you go, and log each removal (path, repo, HEAD SHA, date) in agent-ops BOX-OFFLOAD-LOG.md. If any check fails or ownership is unclear, keep it on disk and list it.

(b) Merge rule. Merge only when GitHub shows the PR as MERGEABLE/CLEAN, every check is verified green through the Actions runs API (a timeout, 403 or unreadable result counts as a FAIL), git diff --diff-filter=D --name-only origin/main...HEAD is empty, and the PR is not freeze-marked. No batch merges: one PR at a time. Claim the work in agent-ops CLAIMS.md first. Never force-push or rebase pushed work. If any check is unverifiable, leave the PR open.

docs.title: Research Conventions (all repos, all agents)
docs.text: Laws: RESEARCH-TO-REPO LAW + CONTINUOUS RESEARCH + PULL-IN LAW (owner 2026-10-16). Owner hates bureaucracy — this is the whole system, keep it this small.

docs.title: Where research docs live
docs.text:
1. Repo-specific findings → that repo's docs/research/. Example: render research → western-heart/docs/research/, teardown tooling → game-reverse-engineering/docs/research/, animation → cape-jones/docs/research/.
  2. Cross-cutting / multi-repo findings → mhvnsnt/agent-ops (this repo is the docs hub). Handoffs, indexes, conventions, manifests.
  3. Never local-only. A research doc that only exists on the VM disk doesn't exist.

docs.title: The master index
docs.text: ~/workspace/agent-ops/RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX.md — one line per topic: | Topic | Date | Doc (repo + path) | Pulled in | Status | Status: researching → wired (installed+tested+green) → excluded (license reason documented). Check the index BEFORE starting new research (./research-check.sh "topic"). A finding without a pull-in is incomplete — track until wired or excluded.

docs.title: Decision records (ADR-lite)
docs.text: For decisions with real consequences (tool choice, format choice, pipeline design), drop a short file in the repo's docs/adr/: docs/adr/0001-short-title.md — template at ~/workspace/agent-ops/adr-template.md. Rules: one decision per file, dated, status line (proposed/accepted/superseded). Never edit a decided ADR — write a new one that supersedes it and link both ways.

docs.title: Research → action pipeline
docs.text: Every research pass ends in one of three states, recorded in the index: 1. Wired — tool pulled in, installed, tested, pushed green (branch → PR → merge). 2. Excluded — documented with the honest license/technical reason (e.g. non-commercial, region-excluded). 3. Queued — finding recorded, pull-in tracked as a work item with an owner.

docs.title: Dedupe
docs.text:
• Before researching: research-check.sh + index search. If it exists, extend it — don't start over.
  • Before pulling: check the index's "Previously pulled" tables. If it's there, wire the existing copy.
  • Source trail survives: every index entry links the doc; every doc links its sources.

docs.title: Cross-referencing (wikilinks)
docs.text: Use [[DOC-NAME]] wikilinks when one doc references another (Zettelkasten pattern: atomic notes, links over folders). They render as plain text on GitHub but are grep-able, so agents and research-check.sh can follow the graph: grep -r "\[\[RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX\]\]" --include="*.md". - The master index is [[RESEARCH-PULLIN-INDEX]] — link it from every research doc's header. - Related docs link each other both ways (A links B, B links A). - Searchable docs site: mkdocs.yml builds this hub with mkdocs-material (full-text search, phone-friendly). Deploys to GitHub Pages via .github/workflows/docs.yml on push to main. Local preview: mkdocs serve. When adding a new root .md, also add its symlink: cd docs && ln -s ../NEW.md . (the CI workflow re-links automatically, but local serve needs it).

docs.title: Resume Brief Template
docs.text: You are resuming a task that was interrupted by a machine/daemon restart. The previous worker is gone. Its checkpoint is your only source of truth.

docs.title: Step 1 — Read these first, in order
docs.text:
1. Your checkpoint: ~/workspace/agent-ops/checkpoints/<TASK_ID>.json
  2. This template (you're reading it)
  3. ~/workspace/agent-ops/IDEMPOTENCY.md — the write rules. Follow them.

docs.title: Step 2 — Reconstruct state
docs.text: From the checkpoint, extract: - Goal: what the task was trying to achieve - Completed steps: already done. DO NOT REDO THESE. Verify cheaply (e.g. ls the output files, git log --oneline -3) instead of re-running. - Next steps: where to continue - Key paths: files and directories the work lives in - Decisions: constraints from earlier in the task. These are binding unless the parent agent explicitly overrides them.

docs.title: Step 3 — Verify before continuing
docs.text:
• Check the repo state: git status --short, git log --oneline -5
  • Check that output files the checkpoint claims exist actually exist
  • If the checkpoint says a step was done but its outputs are missing, treat that step as NOT done and redo it (the restart may have eaten it)

docs.title: Step 4 — Claim the task, then continue with checkpointing
docs.text:
• Claim first: checkpoint.sh claim <TASK_ID> <your-agent-id> — this bumps the fencing epoch and prints EPOCH=N. From now on pass --epoch N on every checkpoint write. If a write comes back FENCED (exit 3), someone else claimed the task after you — stop and report to the parent; do not force your way in. (Full contract: LANE-RESILIENCE-SOP.md.)
  • Update your checkpoint as you work:
  • checkpoint.sh beat <TASK_ID> --epoch N at least every 10 minutes during long runs
  • checkpoint.sh step <TASK_ID> "..." --epoch N after each completed unit of work
  • checkpoint.sh next <TASK_ID> "..." when the plan changes
  • checkpoint.sh decide <TASK_ID> "..." for any decision a future resume needs to know
  • When finished: checkpoint.sh status <TASK_ID> completed
  • If blocked: checkpoint.sh status <TASK_ID> stalled and record why in next_steps

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Never re-push, re-send, or re-publish anything the checkpoint says is done without first verifying it actually landed (check the remote/repo, not memory).
  • If the checkpoint is missing or unreadable, do NOT guess at prior state. Report that to the parent agent and ask for direction.
  • Your final report to the parent must state: what was already done before the restart, what you did after resuming, and what remains.

docs.title: Standing Laws (apply to every resume)
docs.text:
• RESEARCH-BEFORE-ANSWER: If you need to answer "what's the best X", run python3 ~/workspace/tools/research.py compare "<topic>" first. Don't guess from training data.
  • NO-SILENT-FAILURE: If you discover something failed, report it immediately. Never let the owner discover a failure by asking.
  • PHONE-BRIDGE: The owner is phone-only. If something needs a browser/computer, do it yourself. Don't hand him manual homework.
  • PULL-STRAIGHT-TO-STORE: Clone directly into repo checkouts, wire up there, push. Don't stage on local disk.
  • RESPOND-FAST: Acknowledge fast, work async. Don't chain tool calls in silence.
  • CHECK-PR-BODY-LOCALLY: Before opening a PR, verify its body with the local instruction-gate check — the queue's copy at agent-ops/queue-work/instruction_gate-main.py is verified byte-identical to the live gate (.github/scripts/instruction_gate.py on western-heart main). Pattern: agent-ops/queue-work/check1146.py — check(body, changed_files, repo_root, labels, author) returns the error list; empty = pass. A body that fails locally fails CI too, so check before pushing, not after.

docs.title: TorBox Alternatives — Free/Open-Source Research
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-16 | Researcher: subagent | Budget: $0

docs.title: Executive Summary
docs.text:
Key finding: Torrent swarms are DEAD from this VM (verified: 0 peers, 0 bytes in 60s test with libtorrent). This means self-hosted torrent clients (qBittorrent, Transmission, Deluge) CANNOT work here — they need peer connections that the network blocks.

For torrents, the ONLY free path is a remote debrid/seedbox service (they download on their servers, we pull via HTTPS). For everything else, direct HTTP downloads (Internet Archive, GitHub) already work great.

docs.title: 1. Internet Archive (archive.org) — PRIMARY ROUTE ✅
docs.text:
• What: Direct HTTP downloads from archive.org
  • Cost: $0, no account needed
  • API: Yes — https://archive.org/download/<item>/<file>
  • Status: Already the team's primary route, working great
  • Use for: Game ISOs, ROMs, large files hosted on IA

docs.title: 2. GitHub Releases — SECONDARY ROUTE ✅
docs.text:
• What: Direct HTTP downloads from release assets
  • Cost: $0
  • API: Yes — gh CLI + REST API
  • Status: Already heavily used, working great
  • Use for: Tools, extracted files, team deliverables

docs.title: 3. TorBox Free Tier — OWNER'S ACCOUNT ⚠️
docs.text:
• What: Debrid service with permanent free tier
  • Cost: $0 (free tier: 1 slot/day, 10GB/file limit)
  • API: Yes — full REST API, connector at ~/workspace/custom-connectors/custom.torbox/
  • Status: Owner has account, but API returning 401 (credential issue). Owner fixing himself.
  • Note: Local helper scripts had a bug (credential placement changed from bearer_header to query_param). Fixed the scripts, but API still 401s — the stored key itself may be expired.
  • Use for: Torrent → direct link (when working)

docs.title: 4. World-Debrid — 1 Free Debrid/Month 🆓
docs.text:
• URL: https://world-debrid.com/
  • Free tier: 1 debrid per month, permanent. Email or Google signup, NO credit card.
  • What it does: File-hoster links (1fichier, RapidGator, Mega, Turbobit, Uploady, etc.) → direct download links
  • Torrent support: NO — hosters only, not magnets
  • API: Unclear — primarily browser-based
  • Verdict: Useful for file-hoster links, NOT for torrents. Worth the free signup for the 1/month.
  • Action needed: Browser sign-up with Google (fmmg.mars@gmail.com)

docs.title: 5. Seedhost.eu — 24-Hour Free Trial Seedbox 🆓
docs.text:
• URL: https://www.seedhost.eu/
  • Free tier: 24-hour free trial seedbox (they claim "we are the only ones to offer free seedboxes for 24 hours")
  • What it does: Full seedbox — add torrents via web UI, download via HTTPS/FTP
  • API: qBittorrent Web API (standard)
  • Verdict: Good for one-off large torrent pulls. 24h is enough to grab a specific torrent.
  • Action needed: Browser sign-up

docs.title: 6. Pulsed Media — 30-Day Free Trial (When Available) 🆓
docs.text:
• Free tier: 30-day trial (50 GiB storage, 250 MB RAM) "when trial slots are open"
  • What it does: Full seedbox with SSH access
  • Verdict: Best free trial if slots are open. Check availability.
  • Action needed: Browser sign-up, check trial availability

docs.title: ❌ Self-Hosted Torrent Clients on VM
docs.text:
• Tested: libtorrent with real .torrent file (Big Buck Bunny from archive.org)
  • Result: 0 peers, 0 bytes in 60 seconds. Swarm completely unreachable.
  • Why: VM network blocks P2P peer connections (UDP blocked, TCP peers unreachable)
  • Applies to: qBittorrent, Transmission, Deluge, aria2c — all dead for swarms on this VM
  • Note: HTTP trackers are reachable, but no peer connections succeed

docs.title: ❌ Torrin (torrin.app)
docs.text:
• Claimed: "Free tier available"

docs.title: TorBox Breakthrough Program — Final Report (2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Owner order: deep research, all agents on it, find a FREE way to pull the 350GB TorBox file with zero manual phone homework, wire up industry-standard/open-source tooling, and actually finish the pull.

Headline: THE PATH WAS NEVER BLOCKED. The TorBox API key in the Secure Vault is valid and works TODAY. The "BAD_TOKEN" saga was our own connector plumbing: the vault credential is registered with query_param: token placement, so the surrogate is only substituted in a ?token= query parameter. Every Bearer-header call sent the literal hsurr: surrogate to TorBox (correctly rejected as BAD_TOKEN), and every ?token= call to Bearer-only endpoints was ignored (401). The one endpoint family the pull actually needs — requestdl + CDN range reads — works right now, unchanged, on the existing Essential plan. No upgrade, no new key, no owner action.

Lane reports: torbox-lane1-auth.md, torbox-lane2-debrid-live.md, torbox-lane3-alternatives.md, torbox-lane4-compute.md, torbox-lane5-agents.md (+ torbox-lane5-agents/ verbatim outputs), torbox-lane6-oss.md, torbox-lane7-seedbox.md. Prior research built on: TORBOX-RESEARCH-2026-10-19.md (auth conclusions superseded by Lane 1 live evidence), ~/workspace/research_notes/torbox-alternatives-2026-20261016-2150/report.md (web-derived; its TorBox pricing/cap figures were index-grade per its own "Could Not Verify" section and are superseded where live tests conflict).

docs.title: 1. Root cause — proven live, three layers (Lane 1, confirmed by Lane 6 + coordinator)
docs.text:
Live test matrix 2026-10-20, all via the vault surrogate flow, browser UA:

Call Result GET /v1/api/torrents/requestdl?torrent_id=119449922&token=<surrogate> 200, CDN link returned (Lane 1 15:58 UTC; Lane 6 three separate runs; coordinator 4+ runs) CDN link Range: bytes=0-1023 206, PK\x03\x04 ZIP header, Content-Range …/350016069416, Accept-Ranges: bytes CDN tail range 206, ZIP central-directory data GET /v1/api/notifications/rss?token=<surrogate> 200, the account's own feed (Pro trial 2026-10-15, Premium Expired 2026-10-16, Payment Successful 2026-10-18) Bearer surrogate on /user/me, mylist 403 BAD_TOKEN — literal surrogate reached TorBox unsubstituted ?token= on Bearer-only endpoints (mylist) 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"} — query token ignored there Garbage-token control on requestdl (Lane 6) 403 BAD_TOKEN — proves requestdl validates the token; the vault token passes because it is real Unauthenticated /, /v1/api/stats, changelogs 200 through the same egress proxy — proxy/Cloudflare hypothesis dead

Facts established: - Vault entry custom.torbox: name=access_token, type=api_key, placement {"query_param": "token"} (read directly from dynamic_credential_entry metadata, Lane 1 §2). No timestamp fields exist. - Live OpenAPI spec (https://api.torbox.app/openapi.json, 200, 87 paths): sole auth scheme OAuth2PasswordBearer. Only requestdl (torrents/usenet/webdl), notifications/rss, stream/getstreamdata accept ?token=. - The documented Essential 200GB DOWNLOAD_TOO_LARGE limit did not fire on requestdl or range reads of the 350GB file (observed repeatedly). Whether a full single-stream 350GB download would differ is untested and irrelevant — the pipeline is range-based. - No TorBox auth changes after 2026-10-15 (changelog latest v9.2, 2026-08-17; status page clean). No separate "integration token" exists. A live device-code flow (GET /v1/api/user/auth/device/start → 200 unauthenticated) is a fallback token source if the vault key ever truly dies. - Served size for range math: 350,016,069,416 bytes (CDN Content-Range). Note: Lane 6's HEAD on a different CDN host reported Content-Length 350,016,069,757 — CDN nodes appear to report slightly different totals; the extraction pipeline uses each link's own Content-Range total, and all offsets verified against it (CD parsed, extracted file sizes byte-exact).

docs.text:

  2. bin/tb_reqdl.py prints raw requestdl JSON — the CDN URL embeds the real API token. Add token= redaction before anyone runs it outside a pipe.
  3. bin/tb_mylist.py / bin/tb_export.py can never work (query token to Bearer-only endpoints). bin/torbox_add_magnet.py crashes with NameError (calls unimported url_with_surrogate_query_param), verified by Lanes 1, 5, 6.

If Bearer endpoints are ever needed (mylist, createtorrent, integrations): register a SECOND vault entry for the same key with bearer_header placement; leave the working query_param entry untouched. Do NOT regenerate/reset the API key — Lane 6 suggested a reset; that is rejected here: the current token provably authenticates, and regenerating would invalidate the working vault entry (this is very plausibly what started the Oct 15→ failure chain of confusion).

docs.title: Appendix A — Parent-folded deep-research questions (added 2026-10-20, coordinator)
A1. BAD_TOKEN: community reports, key revocation, OAuth/integration tokens, full endpoint groups
docs.text:
• Community/GitHub-issue reports (2025–2026): Lane 1 searched the web and GitHub clients for BAD_TOKEN causes/fixes on 2026-10-20 — results were noise (an unrelated torbox.ch project); no public issue documents this failure mode or a fix. Lane 6 surveyed 342 TorBox-related GitHub repos (official torbox-media-center 284★, atba 180★, DebriDav 155★, DebridDownloader 94★, magnetar 90★, AIOStreams 2,930★, comet 1,120★): every client authenticates with the same single API key; none documents a BAD_TOKEN workaround. The cause in OUR case is proven locally (placement mismatch, §1), not community-sourced: garbage-token control → 403; vault token via ?token= → 200, repeatedly. No TorBox-side auth change exists to blame: official changelog's latest entry is v9.2 (2026-08-17); status page shows no October auth incident (Lane 1 §6).
  • Does generating a new key revoke the old one? No public doc, issue, or changelog entry states the semantics (searched). Indirect evidence supports a single-token model (one refreshtoken operation, rate limits keyed per token, "your API key" singular in settings since v3.0) — under that model a new key replaces the old server-side. BUT it cannot explain our failures: the token in the vault still authenticates today (Lane 1 §3–§4), so whatever the dashboard clicks did, they did not leave us with a dead key. Operational rule from this program: never regenerate the key as a diagnostic — it risks invalidating the one working credential.
  • OAuth / separate integration token? There is NO separate integration token. Token taxonomy (Lane 1 §3, from the live OpenAPI spec + docs): (1) the single API token (Bearer on most endpoints, ?token= on requestdl/rss/ getstreamdata); (2) a web session_token used ONLY to authorize POST /user/refreshtoken and deleteme; (3) OAuth2PasswordBearer is the spec's only security scheme — vendor/third-party apps get OAuth tokens, and TorBox.NET documents refresh as OAuth-only while API-key failures surface as plain BAD_TOKEN; (4) a live device-code flow (GET /v1/api/user/auth/device/start, public, verified 200 today) returns the SAME API token after web authorization — a fallback source, not a distinct credential; (5) presigned CDN tokens embedded in download URLs (~1h per old changelog note).
  • Full endpoint groups (live spec https://api.torbox.app/openapi.json, HTTP 200, 87 paths, fetched again 2026-10-20 by the coordinator): general (stats, changelogs, speedtest, notifications incl. rss Q), user (me, stats, subscriptions, transactions, referral, settings, refreshtoken, deleteme, auth/device/), torrents (createtorrent, asynccreatetorrent, controltorrent, controlqueued, edittorrent, mylist, exportdata, getqueued, checkcached, magnettofile, torrentinfo, requestdl Q), usenet (create/control/edit/mylist/checkcached/provider/, requestdl Q), webdl (create/control/edit/mylist/checkcached/hosters, requestdl Q), queued (GET /v1/api/queued/getqueued, POST /v1/api/queued/controlqueued
  • the torrents/ duplicates), rss (addrss/controlrss/modifyrss/getfeeds/getfeeditems), stream (createstream, getstreamdata Q), integration (cloud-upload jobs — see A2; oauth link/callback/register/ unregister/me; discord linked_roles), vendors (account CRUD). Full per-endpoint auth table: Lane 1 §1.

docs.title: A2. TorBox server-side cloud transfer (Drive/Dropbox/OneDrive)
docs.text: Yes — it exists, as API "integration" jobs (verified from the live OpenAPI spec by the coordinator, 2026-10-20): POST /v1/api/integration/googledrive, /dropbox, /onedrive, /gofile, /pixeldrain, /1fichier; job management GET /integration/jobs, GET /integration/job/{job_id}, GET /integration/jobs/{hash}, DELETE /integration/job/{job_id}. Request shape (spec schemas): for Google Drive, AddToGoogleDrive requires {id (torrent id), google_token} with optional file_id, zip, type (Dropbox identical with dropbox_token) — i.e., you first link the destination cloud via the /integration/oauth/{provider} flow, then TorBox's servers push the downloaded item into it. Limits: the spec states no per-job size limit for integration transfers (the documented DOWNLOAD_TOO_LARGE table governs requestdl, §1); destination quotas govern in practice — free Google Drive is 15GB (owner-established), so Drive is a non-target for a 350GB file regardless. Usability for us: blocked today — every integration endpoint is Bearer-only, and our vault credential substitutes only at query_param placement (§1). Unblocking = the second vault entry with bearer_header placement (parent/vault action, §1 fix #4) plus an OAuth link of the destination cloud (browser lane). The web UI exposes the same feature as "Send to cloud" integrations per the API structure; the dashboard route itself was not browser-verified (parent notes the browser lane is down), so the API evidence above is the verified layer and the UI claim is labeled unverified.

docs.title: A3. Free seedbox trials vs the 350GB single file (Lane 7, official pages fetched 2026-10-20)
docs.text:
• Seedhost.eu: the "24-hour free trial" no longer exists. Current official homepage: all packages are covered by a 7-day money-back policy — order, use, cancel within 7 days for a refund. That requires a payment method, a browser checkout, and a refund claim (Lane 7 file lines 37, 145–146) — it is a purchase + refund gamble, not a free trial, and no current page publishes any trial storage. Paid tiers for scale context: HD 1 = 1TB/€3/mo (NO SSH — FAQ: SSH on all Shared except HD 1); HD 2 = 2TB/€5/mo WITH SSH (rTorrent/ qBittorrent/Deluge/Transmission). HTTPS file access is documented; Range support is NOT published (unverified).
  • Pulsed Media: a real free trial exists — official wiki: 30 days, 50 GiB storage, 250MB RAM, user-level SSH shell (no root), full PMSS feature set, rTorrent/Deluge/qBittorrent, access via SSH/SFTP/SCP/FTP/ HTTPS/WebDAV, Python 3 + p7zip + rclone preinstalled. Card: the trial signup is a WHMCS email signup at pulsedmedia.com/free-seedbox.php — no Google OAuth advertised, and neither source states a card requirement for the FREE trial (labeled: not explicitly verified either way; slot availability is the first gate). Math: 50 GiB is 6.5× too small for the 350GB (326 GiB) file and 2.3× too small for the ~125GB gap set at once; even the free tier's 25%-over-limit burst (62.5 GiB) is ~1.9× short of the gaps. The piece-priority path is technically real (libtorrent over SSH can fetch only pieces covering wanted zip ranges) but cannot fit the wanted pieces under the quota in one pass — only an unproven rotating batch→extract→offload→delete loop could, which is a research project, not a backup path.
  • Others: Ultra.cc explicitly offers NO trials (official FAQ; 7-day refund only). Pulsed's own fetched comparison table lists Whatbox, Feral, Seedboxes.cc, RapidSeedbox, Seedhost, Ultra all as Free Tier: No. Seedbox.io = 14-day money-back only. sdbx.moe = free 2-day trial only via a Discord request (manual), storage unpublished, no ≥100GB evidence.
  • Verdict: the free-trial seedbox angle is DEAD for this torrent. If a seedbox is ever wanted, the cheapest fitting paid shape is Seedhost HD 2 (€5/mo, 2TB + SSH + HTTPS) — an owner purchase decision, stated as fact only. Full evidence: torbox-lane7-seedbox.md.

docs.title: TorBox BAD_TOKEN — Lane 5 All-Agents Review (2026-10-20)
docs.text: Five coding agents were run on the same TorBox review prompt (tb_reqdl.py, tb_mylist.py, tb_export.py, torbox_add_magnet.py, CONNECTOR.md, zip_extract.py). Full verbatim outputs: ~/workspace/agent-ops/torbox-lane5-agents/ (local).

docs.title: Consensus root cause (Copilot CLI + Codex via Kilo gateway, independently)
docs.text:
custom.torbox is registered with bearer_header placement. The authd surrogate (hsurr:...) is only substituted at approved egress points matching that placement — i.e. in an Authorization: Bearer header. tb_reqdl.py manually inserts the surrogate into ?token=:

surrogate = str(entry["surrogate"]).strip()
url = f"https://api.torbox.app/v1/api/torrents/requestdl?torrent_id={tid}&token={quote(surrogate, safe='')}"

TorBox receives the literal surrogate, not the real key -> BAD_TOKEN. This also explains "fresh keys die as BAD_TOKEN": the request never contained the fresh key at all.

docs.title: Additional bugs found
docs.text:
• torbox_add_magnet.py: imports add_surrogate_to_request but calls url_with_surrogate_query_param(...), which is not imported/defined -> NameError before any request is sent (Copilot).
  • tb_mylist.py / tb_export.py / torbox_add_magnet.py call url_with_surrogate_query_param on a bearer_header credential -> Codex (which read the dynamic_credentials module) predicts DynamicCredentialError: credential is not query_param at runtime.
