docs.title: Path B — TorBox Pro (paid fact: $10/mo) — proven-fit fallback
docs.text: Owner already knows TorBox; Pro is the tier that actually fits: 1 TB max per download, 1 TB permanent storage, official API. createtorrent with the magnet → poll mylist → requestdl for the Range-capable direct link. Standard/Essential (200 GB) and Free (10 GB) cannot be used — do not retry them for this file.

docs.title: Path C — Real-Debrid €3 / 15 days (paid, UNPROVEN for this size)
docs.text: Only as an experiment if A and B are rejected: signup at real-debrid.com, €3 tier, API token → instantAvailability first (if cached, it just works); if not cached, addMagnet and watch whether RD will actually ingest a 350 GB torrent. Budget this as a €3 test, not a solution.

docs.title: Recommendation ranking (free-first)
docs.text:
1. PikPak invite trial — free, fits on paper, one shot, 5-day clock, quota risk.
  2. TorBox Pro $10 — not free, but the only documented, API-proven fit in the whole sweep.
  3. Pulsed Media paid seedbox (≥1 TB tier) — full control, Range is self-hosted; free tier is a decoy at 50 GiB.
  4. Everything else: free tiers fail by 7×–350×, or paid tiers are unproven at 350 GB (Premiumize points, Real-Debrid uncached ingestion).

docs.title: Lane 4 — Free compute / cloud-to-cloud transfer layer
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-20 · Status: prototype built + tested locally · No real credential was used anywhere in this lane

docs.title: The problem, restated
docs.text:
A ~350 GB zip sits behind a TorBox dashboard CDN link. Three walls:

  1. Local disk is dead (96–97% full) — nothing more can stage here.
  2. TorBox's API path caps out — API returns BAD_TOKEN; the Essential plan's API allowance (~200 GB) is smaller than the file (350 GB). Dashboard CDN links bypass the API cap, but…
  3. The link itself is a bearer credential, and it is DLP-denylisted as a tool parameter — an agent literally cannot be handed the link through chat tooling.

docs.title: The architecture that dissolves all three walls
docs.text:
Put the compute where the secret can be typed into a platform's own secret store by a human in a browser, and stream through it:

                 pasted ONCE into the platform's secret UI (browser)
                 never in chat / git / agent tool parameters
                                │
                                ▼
 TorBox CDN link ──HTTP Range──► FREE COMPUTE ──pipe──► uploads.github.com
 (350 GB zip,      (tail + CD,   (GHA runner /           ──► private GitHub
  never fully       then only    Kaggle kernel)              release assets
  downloaded)       wanted       RAM: a few MiB              (< 2 GiB each,
                    slices)      Disk: 0 bytes               hash-verified)

Why this works, mechanically:

  • The proven local code already does the hard part. hero-parts-pull/zip_extract.py reads a Zip64 central directory over HTTP Range and fetches only wanted files' byte ranges; hero-parts-pull/github_upload_stream.py pipes a byte stream straight into an uploads.github.com POST and verifies size + head/mid/tail range hashes. Neither needs the whole file, ever.
  • A runner/kernel only needs a few MiB of RAM and zero disk if the extraction is slice-streamed (the local extractor held each file whole in RAM; the prototype fixes that — 1 MiB slices, streaming zlib).
  • The secret problem is a routing problem, not a cryptography problem: GitHub Actions secrets, Kaggle Secrets, Cloudflare secrets, and HF secrets are all entered through that platform's own UI. The value goes browser → platform secret store → runner environment. Chat, agents, and their DLP filters are simply not in the path.
  • Resumability is by construction: release assets are named by content (file name, or slice-<start>-<size>.bin); a re-run skips assets that already exist at the exact size — the same pattern the local uploader uses with its manifest. If a CDN link expires mid-run, paste a fresh link into the secret and re-run; finished slices/files are not redone.

docs.title: Verdict table
docs.text: Platform Verdict Why (evidence below) GitHub Actions ✅ PRIMARY — prototype built Public-repo standard runners: free, no minute cap. Private: 2,000 min/mo free. 14 GB disk is irrelevant (streaming uses 0). 6 h/job cap solved by matrix fan-out (20 concurrent on Free). Secret store is exactly the DLP bypass needed. Same destination platform as the upload target — when target = same repo, not even a PAT is needed. Kaggle kernels ✅ STRONG FALLBACK — variant included Internet-capable kernels, ~9 h sessions, CPU kernels don't touch the 30 GPU-h/week quota, Kaggle Secrets is a real secret store (UserSecretsClient). ~20 GB working cap is irrelevant when streaming out. Weaker than GHA only in automation (kernel push/run is clunkier) and session model. Google Colab ⚠️ Manual fallback only Free runtimes up to 12 h, but idle timeouts (~90 min), no headless trigger, no durable unattended run. Fine if a human is already sitting in the notebook; wrong tool for a 350 GB unattended transfer. Has a Secrets pane (google.colab.userdata) in current Colab — verify in UI. Hugging Face Spaces ⚠️ Workable, awkward Free CPU Basic: 2 vCPU / 16 GB / 50 GB non-persistent disk, secrets as env vars. But a Space is a long-running web app that sleeps, not a batch job — you'd expose a trigger endpoint and babysit it. No advantage over GHA for this job. Cloudflare Workers (free) ❌ Not an engine; ✅ optional proxy Free: 100k req/day but 10 ms CPU/invocation, 128 MB RAM, 50 subrequests. Any Zip64 parsing / zlib / hashing blows the CPU cap. A pure pass-through Range proxy survives (CPU isn't charged while waiting on the network; response body size unenforced) — useful only as URL laundering in front of a real engine. Prototype included, untested live (no CF account wired in this lane). Oracle Always Free ARM 🚩 Owner decision — not recommended by this lane Technically the best always-on free VM (Ampere A1 + 200 GB block). But signup requires a real credit/debit card for identity verification (no prepaid/virtual), home region is permanent, free ARM capacity is frequently unavailable, and idle instances get reclaimed. Spending/identity step = owner's call only, per the brief. MultCloud / cloud-to-cloud services ❌ Dead end for this target Supports ~30–40 clouds (Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, MEGA, FTP/SFTP, WebDAV, S3…) — no TorBox / debrid source, and no GitHub (let alone GitHub Releases) as a target. Its URL "remote upload" lands in a cloud drive, not a release; the obvious free target (Drive, 15 GB) is two orders too small anyway.

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
• Minutes: "GitHub Actions usage is free for standard GitHub-hosted runners in public repositories"; private repos get a plan allowance — 2,000 min/mo on Free, 3,000 Pro/Team, 50,000 Enterprise Cloud. (GitHub plans doc; billing summary)
  • Runner: Linux standard runner = 14 GB SSD (2 vCPU/8 GB private, 4 vCPU/16 GB public per the current runner table). Our streaming peak disk is the checkout (< 1 MB) — the 14 GB never binds. (runner reference)
  • Job cap: each job max 6 hours execution; timeout-minutes max
  • Concurrency: Free plan = 20 concurrent jobs. (Actions limits) → Fan-out math (scenarios, not measurements — runner bandwidth was not benchmarked in this lane): one job must move its share in < 6 h, i.e. sustain ≥ share/21,600 s. A full 350 GB mirror split 20 ways = 17.5 GB per job ≈ 0.81 MB/s floor per job — a very low bar. The selective pull (the ~5 GB actually wanted in past pulls of this kind) is a single short job at any plausible speed.
  • Release asset cap: each release file must be < 2 GB (2 GiB). The workflow defaults to the owner's 100 MB asset standard (slice_size=100000000) and accepts anything < 2 GiB. (storage limits write-up; gh-large-releases, built around the same 2 GB limit)
  • Secrets: entered in repo Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions; injected as env; GitHub masks exact secret values in logs. This prototype additionally never prints the URL (scheme + host + path only, query redacted) and never puts it on a command line.
  • The unlimited-minutes shape: make the runner repo public (code only — it contains no data and no secrets in git) and the target repo private, reached with a fine-grained PAT stored as a secret in the runner repo (scope: that one repo, Contents: Read and write, short expiry). Public minutes are free; the assets land private. If the target release may live in the runner repo itself, skip the PAT entirely — the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN with permissions: contents: write suffices.
  • ⚠️ Terms flag (read before the first big run): GitHub's Actions terms restrict uses unrelated to the repo's own software project (bulk file-hosting / distribution abuse is the classic enforcement case). This lane's honest read: streaming this project's own assets into this project's own releases is project-scoped CI-shaped work, and the selective pull is small. A repeated wholesale 350 GB mirror through a public repo is greyer and higher-profile. Keep runs project-scoped and modest, prefer the private-repo/2,000-min path when the job fits it, and treat any GitHub warning as a stop signal. This is a judgement call for the owner, surfaced — not hidden.

docs.title: Kaggle
docs.text:
• Kernels: CPU notebooks (4 cores / ~16 GB in secondary sources), GPU quota 30 h/week (owner-known), sessions up to ~9 h, saved output capped ~20 GB, internet is a notebook setting that must be ON. (Kaggle constraints summary; notebook resource notes)
  • Secrets: Add-ons → Secrets; read with from kaggle_secrets import UserSecretsClient / UserSecretsClient().get_secret("SOURCE_URL") — same DLP bypass shape as GHA. (GitGuardian on notebook secrets)
  • Use CPU kernels for byte moving; GPU quota is for renders. Variant script: torbox-gha-prototype/kaggle/kaggle_kernel.py.

docs.title: Cloudflare Workers
docs.text:
• Free plan, from Cloudflare's own docs: 100,000 requests/day, 10 ms CPU time, 128 MB memory, 50 subrequests/request, 6 simultaneous outgoing connections; request body cap 100 MB on the Free zone plan; response body size not enforced. (Workers limits; Workers pricing)
  • Conclusion drawn from those numbers: a Worker can proxy a Range stream (I/O wait is not CPU time) but cannot be the engine — parsing a central directory, inflating deflate streams, and SHA-256 over gigabytes inside 10 ms CPU slices is not a thing. Optional proxy prototype: torbox-gha-prototype/cloudflare-worker/worker.js.

docs.title: Colab / HF Spaces
docs.text:
• Colab free: notebooks run at most 12 hours, idle timeouts apply, availability varies. (Colab FAQ)
  • HF Spaces free CPU Basic: 2 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, 50 GB non-persistent disk; secrets configured per-Space and exposed as env vars; free Spaces sleep when idle. (Spaces overview)

docs.title: Oracle Always Free
docs.text:
• Ampere A1 ARM + 200 GB block storage, always-free — but signup states, in every current guide: a valid credit card is required for identity verification; virtual/prepaid cards are not accepted; a small temporary hold is placed; the home region chosen at signup is permanent for Always Free resources. (setup guide; 2026 limits write-up)
  • Flagged, not recommended. If the owner ever chooses to create the account himself, an always-on ARM box becomes the cleanest engine of all (no 6 h cap, no minute accounting) — the same range_list.py runs there unchanged. Nobody else should make that signup call.

docs.title: MultCloud
docs.text:
• Supported set is mainstream cloud drives + FTP/SFTP/WebDAV/NAS/S3 (~30–40 services). TorBox is not among them; GitHub is not among them. (MultCloud supported clouds; MultCloud intro, supported list)
  • No source, no target → no path. Closed.

docs.title: One more dead end, stated plainly
docs.text: Magnet-direct is not viable at 350 GB on any free tier above. A torrent client must land the bytes somewhere before re-chunking them; every free disk here is 14–50 GB. The only shapes that work at this size are (a) Range-selective extraction of wanted files, and (b) Range re-chunking of the raw archive — both need the HTTP/CDN link, which is exactly what the secret-store architecture delivers. (For a small wanted subset, torrent file-selection on Kaggle's ~20 GB would fit — fallback B, only if no CDN link can be obtained at all.)

docs.title: The prototype
docs.text:
~/workspace/agent-ops/torbox-gha-prototype/ — README, workflow, range_list.py (stdlib only), Kaggle variant, Worker proxy, test evidence. Design deltas vs the local originals:

  • CD parsed incrementally (8 MiB fetches, carry buffer) — no whole-CD or whole-file RAM residency anywhere.
  • extract-one verifies CRC32 against the central directory (the local script never checked).
  • slice mode is a stdout generator for raw re-chunking: range_list.py slice <start> <size> | curl --data-binary @- …uploads…
  • URL only from SOURCE_URL env; logs print scheme+host+path with the query redacted; size discovery falls back from HEAD to a bytes=0-0 probe for signed links that reject HEAD.

docs.title: Test evidence (local, public file, 2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Target: the archive.org Zip64 zip OK KO.zip, 7,910,137,932 bytes — previously parsed by the local pipeline (hero-parts-pull/okko-ia-centraldir.json), so results cross-check.

Test Result list 476 entries / 428 files / 12.046 GB uncompressed — matches the earlier independent parse (476 entries, 7,910,137,932 bytes) exactly extract-one ENID_01_RGB.ai 444,118 bytes streamed out; size_ok=True; CRC32 computed 4843a44f == CD CRC 4843a44f; sha256 2245c7c3…a973a slice 1000000 4194304 sha256 b8103775…c519 — byte-identical to an independent curl -L -r fetch of the same range

Logs: torbox-gha-prototype/test-output/ (list-run.log, extract-one-run.log, slice-crosscheck.txt, okko-manifest.json). YAML and both Python files pass syntax checks; worker.js passes node --check.

Not tested (needs the parent/browser lane): an actual Actions run, and Range behaviour of a real TorBox CDN link. Both are first-run smoke items, deliberately sequenced: mode=list costs only ~70 KB + the CD bytes and answers "does this link honour Range after redirects?" before a single big byte moves.

docs.title: Runbook for the parent / browser lane
docs.text:
1. Create the runner repo with this prototype's code (public for unlimited minutes, or private if the job fits 2,000 min/mo and you prefer it — selective pulls fit easily). Push via the normal branch → PR → merge path. No secrets in git, ever.
  2. In that repo: Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions — add secret SOURCE_URL (paste the TorBox dashboard CDN link in the browser), and, for a separate private target repo, secret TARGET_PAT + variables TARGET_REPO, RELEASE_TAG.
  3. Actions → torbox-range → Run workflow → mode=list. Expect the manifest artifact + entry count in the log. If Range fails here, the link/CDN is the problem — nothing else was spent.
  4. Then mode=extract-one per wanted file, or mode=slice-upload with the JSON offset list for a whole-archive mirror (100 MB assets by default; 20-way matrix max).
  5. Verify per the workflow's built-in checks (upload size-exact; the extract pass prints CRC OK before the upload pass runs).
  6. Cleanup: delete SOURCE_URL / revoke TARGET_PAT when done. Bearer link + PAT are spent once the transfer lands.

docs.title: Open questions / risks
docs.text:
• TorBox CDN link lifetime and Range-after-redirect behaviour: unproven until runbook step 3. Mitigation is built in (resumable assets, cheap smoke test first).
  • GHA bandwidth from runner → TorBox CDN and runner → uploads endpoint was not benchmarked here; the 6 h math has huge headroom at 20-way fan-out, but the first real run should record its own throughput in the run log for the next plan.
  • Actions terms flag (above) — owner's call on public-vs-private runner repo for the big mirror; selective pulls are low-profile either way.
  • Kaggle internet-on kernels and the Colab Secrets pane are settings-level facts from secondary sources — confirm in the UI at setup time; neither blocks the GHA primary path.

docs.title: Lane 5 — All-Agents Tooling on TorBox BAD_TOKEN (2026-10-20)
docs.text: Evidence dir: torbox-lane5-agents/ (one file per agent, verbatim outputs). Same review prompt was given to every runnable agent: review tb_reqdl.py, tb_mylist.py, tb_export.py, torbox_add_magnet.py, CONNECTOR.md, zip_extract.py for the requestdl ?token= / BAD_TOKEN bug. No secrets printed (COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN checked by existence/length only: present in ~/.bashrc, 93 chars).

docs.title: Inventory corrections to the brief
docs.text:
• opencode DID survive: ~/.local/bin/opencode v1.19.3 — it was just missing from this shell's PATH (~/.local/bin not in PATH), so which missed it.
  • codex v0.149.0 at /opt/hatch-image/bin/codex. gh 2.102.0, logged in as mhvnsnt.
  • Copilot CLI and Kilo CLI binaries did NOT survive the VM swap (config/state did: ~/.copilot with mhvnsnt logged in, ~/.config/kilo + ~/.local/share/kilo). Both were reinstalled via npm during this lane.
  • aider / cline / gemini: not on PATH (unchanged).

docs.title: 1. Copilot CLI — ✅ RAN, full review (copilot.txt)
docs.text: Reinstalled: npm i -g @github/copilot → GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.100 at /usr/bin/copilot. Ran non-interactively with COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN sourced from ~/.bashrc (value never logged). Findings: - Root cause (likely): tb_reqdl.py sends the authd surrogate to TorBox as if it were the API key — lines 15–17 extract entry["surrogate"] and insert it into ?token=, with no Authorization header and no credential exchange. A surrogate is a broker-specific substitute, not a TorBox key; with bearer_header registration, manually moving it into token is the bug. Fresh keys failing doesn't rule this out — the request still wouldn't contain the fresh key. - Ranked the other hypotheses low: URL-encoding is correct (quote(..., safe='')), path/order fine, redirect refusal would traceback not BAD_TOKEN, UA already set (Cloudflare 1010 ≠ BAD_TOKEN), plan cap would not be an auth error. - New bug found: torbox_add_magnet.py imports add_surrogate_to_request but calls url_with_surrogate_query_param(...), which is not imported or defined → NameError before any request. (Verified by reading the file in this lane.) - Diagnostic sequence: baseline via tb_mylist.py → retry requestdl through the broker's supported query_param placement → capture status/body/redirect with token redacted → only then check plan/caps. Do NOT regenerate the key as a diagnostic. - Caveat it stated itself: zip_extract.py access was denied in its sandbox, so it made no finding on that file; diagnosis is "strong, not proof" without the dynamic_credentials helper source.

docs.title: 2. Codex — ⚠️ direct lane 401; ✅ full review via Kilo gateway (codex.txt, codex-kilo.txt)
docs.text:
• Direct OpenAI lane: still broken. Exact error (codex.txt): failed to connect to websocket: HTTP error: 401 Unauthorized, url: wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses and unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Missing bearer or basic authentication in header. Retried 5× then fell back; run was cut at timeout with the 401 already definitive.
  • Via Kilo Code free gateway (codex -p kilo-code exec, model openrouter/free, provider kilo-code): worked (sanity test CODEX_KILO_OK, then full review, 135,195 tokens). It read the actual dynamic_credentials module, so its diagnosis is the most specific:
  • Root cause confirmed by code: surrogate substitution only happens for the registered placement. custom.torbox is bearer_header; Sentinel/authd substitutes hsurr:... only in Authorization: Bearer. tb_reqdl.py:17-18 puts the literal surrogate in ?token= → TorBox sees the surrogate → BAD_TOKEN.
  • More bugs: tb_mylist.py:13, tb_export.py:12, torbox_add_magnet.py:34 all call url_with_surrogate_query_param on a bearer_header credential → predicted DynamicCredentialError: credential is not query_param at runtime (i.e. the "working" helpers would crash before sending, unless the credential was re-registered).
  • Fix A (preferred if requestdl accepts Bearer): use add_surrogate_to_request, drop &token=. Fix B (if ?token= truly required): register a second entry with {"query_param": "token"} placement and use url_with_surrogate_query_param everywhere.
  • Diagnostic sequence with expected outcomes for each step (placement print → tb_mylist crash test → Bearer-surrogate requestdl test).

Consensus: Copilot and Codex/Kilo independently converged on the same root cause (surrogate in ?token= never substituted for a bearer_header credential). That also explains the "every fresh key dies as BAD_TOKEN" saga: the failing requests never contained any real key.

docs.title: 3. Kilo — ⚠️ native CLI blocked; gateway contributed (kilo.txt, codex-kilo.txt)
docs.text: Reinstalled: npm i -g @kilocode/cli → kilo 7.8.15 at /usr/bin/kilo (kilo --help works). - Native kilo run "<review prompt>": Error: "You need to sign in to use this model." It defaulted to google/gemini-3-pro-image (stale session/model state), not the kilo-free config in ~/.config/kilo (config.json defines kilo-free/openrouter/free, but Kilo 7.8 logs a V1-compat warning that drops the providers block). - kilo run -m kilo-free/openrouter/free "Reply exactly: KILO_OK": timed out at 90s, no output (EXIT:124). - kilo auth list: timed out at 30s, no output. - Workflow-law exception invoked for the NATIVE binary: evidence above. BUT Kilo did contribute — the entire Codex review above ran on Kilo Code's free gateway (api.kilo.ai, openrouter/free, 200 req/hr/IP per the 2026-10-16 arsenal doc).

docs.title: 4. OpenCode — ❌ binary OK, runs never complete (opencode.txt)
docs.text: ~/.local/bin/opencode v1.19.3; --help/--version fine. Three opencode run attempts (full review prompt; short prompt with -m opencode/big-pickle ×2): each starts (> build · big-pickle) and produces no completion within 110–300s, killed by timeout (EXIT:124). No provider is configured in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc (empty schema-only file). Workflow-law exception: binary present and launching, model calls stall in this VM; no review output obtained. Evidence in opencode.txt.

docs.title: 5. CodeRabbit — ⚠️ triggered on PR #36, no review received yet (coderabbit-pr.txt)
docs.text:
• No open TorBox PR existed in mhvnsnt/agent-ops (17 open PRs checked, none TorBox).
  • Created branch docs/torbox-lane5-agent-review-20261020 (fresh /tmp clone — the local agent-ops checkout is dirty on another PR branch and was not touched), added TORBOX-LANE5-AGENT-REVIEW-2026-10-20.md with the consensus findings, opened PR #36: https://github.com/mhvnsnt/agent-ops/pull/36 with @coderabbitai review in the body, plus an explicit @coderabbitai review comment (comment id 6296484877).
  • After ~10 minutes: no CodeRabbit comment/review on the PR (only mhvnsnt's trigger comment; reviews list empty). No .coderabbit.yaml in the repo, and gh pr checks is blocked by PAT scope ("Resource not accessible by personal access token"), so CodeRabbit's app installation on this repo could not be verified from here. Honest status: trigger delivered, review not (yet) produced — likely the CodeRabbit GitHub App is not installed/enabled on mhvnsnt/agent-ops.

docs.title: Bottom line for the TorBox problem
docs.text: Two independent agents, one of which read the credential-broker source, agree: stop putting the surrogate in ?token=. Next step is the 3-step diagnostic in the PR doc (placement print → tb_mylist crash test → Bearer-surrogate requestdl), then Fix A or B depending on whether requestdl accepts Bearer.

docs.title: TorBox Lane 6 — Open-Source Wire-Up + Testing
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-20 (CDT). All TorBox API tests ran through the Secure Vault surrogate flow only (dynamic_credentials, credential custom.torbox); no key was hardcoded, printed, or logged. Surrogates appear below only as <SURR>. CDN URLs are never printed, only their hostnames.

docs.title: HEADLINE FINDING — the BAD_TOKEN wall is endpoint-shaped, not total
docs.text:
The stored TorBox key is dead for Bearer-authenticated endpoints but requestdl works today through the ?token= query flow. Evidence (2026-10-20, torrent 119449922 "Documents", the 350GB cached torrent from CONNECTOR.md):

Call Auth style Result GET /v1/api/torrents/mylist (raw helper bin/tb_mylist.py) ?token=<SURR> appended by helper HTTP 401 {"detail":"Not authenticated"} (mylist does not accept query-token auth at all) GET mylist probe Authorization: Bearer <SURR> only HTTP 403 {"success":false,"error":"BAD_TOKEN","detail":"Your token is invalid or has expired..."} GET mylist probe Bearer + ?token= HTTP 403 BAD_TOKEN (same) GET /v1/api/user/me probe Bearer only HTTP 403 BAD_TOKEN GET /v1/api/user/me probe ?token= only HTTP 401 Not authenticated GET /v1/api/torrents/requestdl?torrent_id=119449922&zip_link=true (helper bin/tb_reqdl.py) ?token=<SURR> only HTTP 200 {"success":true,"detail":"Torrent download requested successfully.","data":"<CDN URL>"} Same via torbox-api SDK request_download_link Bearer + ?token= (SDK sends both) 200, success=True, data= requestdl probe Bearer only, no ?token= HTTP 422 missing query token (endpoint requires the query param) requestdl probe ?token=GARBAGE_NOT_A_TOKEN (control) HTTP 403 BAD_TOKEN — so requestdl does validate the token; the surrogate swap delivers a token requestdl accepts

Conclusion: Sentinel swaps the surrogate in the query string too, and the resulting token passes requestdl's validation while failing Bearer validation on mylist/user/me. Whatever the server-side reason (token scope/rotation state), the practical pipeline consequence is:

requestdl → CDN link works NOW. Listing/profile/createtorrent-style Bearer endpoints do not. The pipeline only needs requestdl for torrents already on the account (id known: 119449922), so the range-extract lane is unblocked for that torrent. Adding NEW torrents (createtorrent is Bearer) stays blocked until the owner resets the API token in TorBox settings and the vault credential is re-registered.

docs.title: CONNECTOR.md corrections (noted, not edited — additive-only rule)
docs.text:
• Stored credential placement is actually {"query_param": "token"} (verified from dynamic_credential_entry("custom.torbox")), not bearer_header as the doc states.
  • bin/tb_reqdl.py is NOT broken: it returned 200 + CDN link in this run. The doc's "Untested / broken" section is stale.
  • Existing helpers (tb_mylist.py, tb_export.py, torbox_add_magnet.py) already use url_with_surrogate_query_param; mylist still fails because that endpoint ignores query tokens and wants Bearer (403 BAD_TOKEN).

docs.title: 1. torbox-api Python SDK (PyPI torbox-api 1.0.6, MIT)
docs.text:
Installed into a throwaway venv (pip install torbox-api, 20MB incl. requests; venv lived in /tmp and was wiped by another lane's /tmp cleanup after testing — reinstall is one command).

Source inspection (torbox_api/): - TorboxApi(access_token) fans the token out to 9 services; auth is AccessTokenAuth → Authorization: Bearer <token> on every call. - services/torrents.py::request_download_link is the one difference from raw calls: its serializer attaches the Bearer header AND .add_query("token", token) — dual auth. That matches the API: requestdl requires ?token= (422 without it). - Transport is plain requests.request with no browser User-Agent (default python-requests UA) and no redirect control. It survived Cloudflare here (no 1010), but CONNECTOR.md's browser-UA rule remains the safer default for raw calls. - Error handling drops response bodies: on HTTP ≥400 it raises RequestError with status only — the BAD_TOKEN detail body is lost, which makes debugging worse than the raw helpers. - Base URL default https://api.torbox.app, timeout default 60000ms.

Live tests (surrogate as access_token, output scrubbed): - api.torrents.get_torrent_list(api_version="v1") → RequestError 403 (Bearer BAD_TOKEN, same as raw probe). - api.torrents.request_download_link(api_version="v1", token=<SURR>, torrent_id="119449922", zip_link="true") → RequestDownloadLinkOkResponse(success=True, detail="Torrent download requested successfully.", data=<CDN URL>).

Verdict: SDK does nothing the raw helpers don't, except dual-auth requestdl — and tb_reqdl.py already achieves the same 200 with the query flow alone. Not adopted (extra dependency, worse errors, no UA control). The dual-auth detail is documented here in case a future endpoint wants both.

docs.title: 2. rclone v1.75.2 (genuine, off-PATH)
docs.text:
• Binary: ~/workspace/tools/rclone/rclone (82MB, static, go1.26.9). rclone version → rclone v1.75.2, ubuntu 24.04, linux/amd64. Not on PATH (rclone: command not found in a bare shell).
  • rclone help backends on this build: no torbox, no realdebrid, no alldebrid backend. rclone help backend realdebrid → CRITICAL: didn't find backend called "realdebrid".
  • The one debrid backend present: premiumizeme (premiumize.me, OAuth client_id/secret). Also adjacent: fichier (1Fichier), putio, http, webdav, internetarchive, mega, pikpak.
  • Dummy-config test (--config /tmp/.../rclone-test.conf, no secrets): listremotes works; an http remote against a local server listed and rclone cat streamed a file fine — rclone's http/webdav remotes are the usable glue shapes.
  • Pipeline role: rclone cannot talk to TorBox directly. It can sit downstream of anything that exposes WebDAV/HTTP (Decypharr's WebDAV, TorBox's own WebDAV — existence attested by TorBox Media Center README "use TorBox's WebDAV"; endpoint/credentials NOT verified in this lane), and it is Decypharr's own mount engine (pkg/rclone, RC port 5572). For the single-zip range-extract job it adds nothing over zip_extract.py, which already speaks Range to the CDN directly.

docs.title: 3. Decypharr (sirrobot01/decypharr — 917★, MIT, Go, repo 20.6MB)
docs.text:
Clone into /tmp was attempted and aborted on a transient /tmp-full condition; inspection was done from the GitHub API + raw sources instead (no long service was run, per task).

  • Providers (README + pkg/debrid/providers/): Real-Debrid, TorBox, DebridLink, AllDebrid, Premiumize + direct Usenet/NNTP. Mock qBittorrent/SABnzbd APIs for the *Arr stack; serves via its own DFS VFS, embedded/external rclone mounts, NFSv4/SMB, and built-in WebDAV (docs.decypharr.com: "mounts remote files using DFS, Rclone, or serves via WebDAV").
  • Auth: config debrids[].api_key (config.full.json shape: name/host/api_key/folder/rate_limit/...). Its TorBox provider (pkg/debrid/providers/torbox/torbox.go) sends Authorization: Bearer <api_key> with a custom UA and a built-in 300 req/min limiter (comment cites TorBox's per-key cap). Same BAD_TOKEN wall: its mylist/user-me calls would 403 with the current key exactly like our probes.
  • Download links: fetchDownloadLink makes no API call — it builds the permalink https://api.torbox.app/v1/api/torrents/requestdl?token= <account token>&torrent_id=<id>&file_id=<fid>&redirect=true, i.e. the exact query-token flow proven working above. Its SpeedTest reads Range: bytes=0-1048575 from that link, i.e. Decypharr itself assumes TorBox CDN links honor Range.
  • HTTP Range for zip_extract: Decypharr's WebDAV/VFS is a streaming media layer; feeding a 350GB zip through it to range-extract would add a daemon, a FUSE/WebDAV hop, and an Arr-shaped cache in front of a job zip_extract.py already does directly against the CDN URL. Verdict: real, maintained, production-grade — but not needed for this pipeline, and TorBox-side it is blocked by the same dead Bearer key for everything except the requestdl permalink trick it shares with our helper. Revisit if an *Arr/media-serving need appears or after the token is reset (then it becomes the strongest off-the-shelf TorBox mount: it would give rclone a WebDAV target).

docs.title: 4. JDownloader2 headless — SKIP (feasibility only)
docs.text:
• Headless route is the jlesage/docker-jdownloader-2 image or a bare JVM run: JDOWNLOADER_HEADLESS=1 + -Djava.awt.headless=true, and in headless mode MyJDownloader (cloud account, email+password) is the only control interface.
  • This VM: java: command not found, no /usr/lib/jvm, no Docker on PATH, ~8GB RAM mostly committed, root disk 94–97% full. Installing a JVM + JD2 (+ its self-updating jar churn) to gain a whole-file downloader is negative value: JD2 has no remote-zip Range extraction, no TorBox-specific advantage over the working requestdl→CDN path, and its debrid handling still needs the same account credentials.
  • Skipped with reason: heavy Java stack, extra cloud account, wrong tool shape (full downloads, not range-extract).

docs.title: 5. aria2 1.35.0 (~/workspace/tools/aria2/aria2c wrapper)
docs.text:
Wrapper sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the bundled libs; the bare usr/bin/aria2c fails without it (libaria2.so.0: cannot open shared object file) — always call the wrapper.

  • HTTP(S) multi-connection: works. Local test: aria2c --max-connection-per-server=4 --split=4 http://127.0.0.1:18222/src.txt → status OK, content verified byte-for-byte (lane6-aria2-http-test). Useful as a parallel downloader for plain CDN/HTTP files.
  • Magnet: dead from this VM, re-verified today. aria2c --bt-metadata-only=true 'magnet:?xt=urn:btih:856d0103…&dn=Documents' ran 25s at 0 B/s, stayed INPR [MEMORY][METADATA], fetched no metadata, no peers. Consistent with the 2026-10-17 finding (outbound UDP/DHT blocked; see ~/workspace/hero-parts-pull/swarm_check.py, libtorrent DHT test built for exactly this hash). aria2 magnet only becomes viable via a seedbox/remote node that hands back an HTTP URL — which is precisely what a debrid's requestdl already does.
  • Role: fine as an HTTP download accelerator downstream of a CDN link; zip_extract.py + GitHub streaming upload already cover the actual job with range precision aria2 doesn't offer for zip members.

docs.title: 6. New / notable 2025–2026 open-source TorBox tools (GitHub API search, 2026-10-20)
docs.text:
Search torbox: 342 repos; torbox created:>2024-06-01: 316; debrid created:>2024-06-01: 711. Relevant finds (stars as of today):

Repo ★ Auth / shape Fit sirrobot01/decypharr 917 per-provider api_key in config; Bearer for TorBox See §3 TorBox-App/torbox-media-center 284 official TorBox team; TORBOX_API_KEY env; Python, MIT; FUSE/.strm mount, video files only, paid plan required, read-only; explicitly defers to TorBox's own WebDAV Media serving only; same key wall (Bearer mylist); not a zip/range tool jittarao/torbox-app 184 alternative TorBox web UI UI only 93Pd9s8Jt/atba 180 cross-platform TorBox client (Dart, GPL-3.0), streaming Desktop client; API key skjaere/DebriDav 155 Kotlin, MIT; WebDAV bridge for debrids + Arr stack Same family as Decypharr; smaller CasaVargas/DebridDownloader 94 Rust/Tauri desktop, GPL-3.0; RD + TorBox + Premiumize; resumable multi-connection; tokens in OS keychain (the orion01500/DebridDownloader fork shows 0★ — use upstream) Desktop whole-file downloader; no range-extract ArrCee76/magnetar 90 browser extension: send magnets to RD/TorBox/AllDebrid/Premiumize/local client Ingest convenience only Viren070/AIOStreams 2930 Stremio addon aggregator (debrid-backed streaming) Streaming, not extraction g0ldyy/comet 1120 Stremio torrent/debrid addon Streaming, not extraction

None of the 2025–2026 crop changes the auth picture: every TorBox tool authenticates with the account API key (Bearer for API calls, ?token= for requestdl permalinks). No tool bypasses a dead key, and none offers remote-zip range extraction — that remains our zip_extract.py's job, by design.

docs.title: 7. CDN Range verification (the zip_extract contract)
docs.text:
Proven-path evidence already on disk: the earlier successful extraction ran zip_extract.py against a TorBox CDN URL (~/workspace/hero-parts-pull/dlurl.txt, host nexus-088.cnam.tb-cdn.io) — log okko-extract.log: zip size: 350.0 GB, zip64 central dir: 79772 entries, parsed 79772 entries. So TorBox CDN links honor HEAD + Range and the 350GB zip's central directory was already pulled this way.

Fresh-link probe (2026-10-20, new helper bin/tb_cdn_range_probe.py, torrent 119449922, run three times — requestdl succeeded every time): - requestdl success: True | detail: Torrent download requested successfully. - cdn host: store-013.wnam.tb-cdn.io - HEAD -> 200 | len: 350016069757 | accept-ranges: bytes | type: application/zip (350,016,069,757 = the zip_link wrapper; the inner Documents.zip listed in CONNECTOR.md is 350,016,069,428.) - The probe's two small Range GETs did not return within the lane's 125s window (CDN first-byte latency from this VM; no HTTP error was returned — the calls hung, they were not refused). Range support is nonetheless established: Accept-Ranges: bytes on the fresh link, Decypharr's Range-based SpeedTest design, and above all the prior full extraction, which ran entirely on zip_extract.py's assert r.status == 206 Range fetches against a tb-cdn.io link. A patient re-run of the probe (it allows 60s per call) is the way to re-confirm Range reads on a fresh link; nothing about the timeout contradicts the contract.

docs.title: Winners wired
docs.text:
1. Kept/winner: existing pipeline — bin/tb_reqdl.py (query-token requestdl, verified 200 today) → CDN URL → zip_extract.py (Range) → github_upload_stream.py. No new dependency needed.
  2. Added (additive, connector dir): bin/tb_cdn_range_probe.py — one-command health check of the whole contract (requestdl success, CDN host, HEAD length/Accept-Ranges, head+tail Range reads) that prints no URLs or secrets.
  3. Not adopted: torbox-api SDK (§1), Decypharr (§3, revisit after token reset), JDownloader2 (§4), rclone-as-TorBox-client (no such backend, §2), aria2-for-magnets (§5).
  4. Owner action that unblocks everything else: reset the TorBox API token in TorBox settings and re-register the custom.torbox vault credential. Bearer endpoints (mylist, createtorrent, user/me) are 403 BAD_TOKEN until then; requestdl already works.

docs.title: Lane 7 — Free-Trial Seedbox Angle (Seedhost.eu + Pulsed Media + others)
docs.text: Date: 2026-10-20 (researched live this session) Target: Documents.zip — ONE file, 350,016,069,428 B (= 350.0 GB decimal = ~326 GiB) Infohash: 856d01039553693d51c2a98523ca2c9829e8bb63 Actual need: ~125 GB of gap ranges INSIDE the zip. Because the torrent is a single file, qBittorrent/ruTorrent file priorities cannot skip inner zip entries — the only seedbox-side selective paths are (a) hold the whole file, or (b) shell/SSH + a custom client (libtorrent piece priorities) that only fetches the pieces covering the wanted byte ranges.

docs.title: VERDICT: DEAD for this torrent as a free-trial path
docs.text:
No free trial found holds the file, and none holds even the wanted ranges at once. Numbers:

Candidate Free trial (verified) Trial storage SSH/shell on trial? vs 350 GB full vs ~125 GB gaps-at-once Pulsed Media 30-day free, when slots open 50 GiB, 250 MB RAM YES — user-level SSH, full PMSS set FAIL 6.5× (326 GiB needed) FAIL 2.3× (~116 GiB needed) Seedhost.eu NO free trial on current site — 7-day money-back on PAID plans only n/a (old 24 h trial no longer offered; its size was never published) Paid: SSH on all Shared except HD 1 FAIL — nothing free to hold it FAIL Ultra.cc No trials at all (official FAQ) — — FAIL FAIL Whatbox / Feral / Seedboxes.cc / RapidSeedbox No free tier (Pulsed comparison table) — — FAIL FAIL Seedbox.io No free trial — 14-day money-back only — — FAIL FAIL sdbx.moe Free 2-day trial on Discord request Not published, no ≥100 GB evidence Unknown FAIL / unproven, and Discord request = manual work FAIL

This lane is backup-path verification only — the TorBox direct path (requestdl + CDN ranges) already works per the other lane. Nothing here beats it, and nothing here is worth the browser lane's time.

docs.title: 1. Seedhost.eu — the "24-hour free trial" no longer exists
docs.text:
• Current official homepage (fetched this session, https://www.seedhost.eu): under "NEED A TRIAL ACCOUNT?" it now says: "All our hosting packages are covered with 7 days money back policy. You can order any of our account and use it as a test, you can cancel it with the first 7 days and we will refund your money." That is a paid order + refund, not a free trial: it needs a payment method, a browser checkout, and a refund claim.
  • Pulsed Media's competitor comparison (fetched this session) corroborates: Seedhost.eu — Free Tier: No, Refund Period: 7 days, clients rTorrent/Deluge/qBittorrent/Transmission.
  • The "only ones to offer free seedboxes for 24 hours" line survives only in old third-party site mirrors (technofizi.net crawl of the old site copy) and a ~2012 press release (sbwire). No current Seedhost page publishes a trial size — there is nothing to verify ≥350 GB against, because there is no trial to size.
  • Paid plans (official, fetched https://www.seedhost.eu/shared-app-hosting/): HD 1 = 1 TB disk / 1 TB traffic / €3/mo (no SSH — FAQ: "Yes, we offer SSH access with all Shared App Hosting accounts, except HD 1"; no root on Shared); HD 2 = 2 TB / 2 TB traffic / €5/mo with SSH, "welcome to install anything locally via SSH in your HOME path." Apps include rTorrent/ruTorrent, qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission.
  • So a paid HD 2 (€5) would fit the full 350 GB with shell access — but that is a purchase, not this lane's free-trial question, and it still requires the (currently flaky) browser lane for checkout.
  • HTTPS file access: files are served via the account web space / apps (e.g. additional web users via .htaccess, per Seedhost knowledgebase). HTTP Range support is not documented/published — UNVERIFIED. SFTP/FTP access is documented (their migration KB references FTP/SSH access).

docs.title: 2. Pulsed Media — real free trial, real shell, 7× too small
docs.text:
Official wiki, fetched this session (https://wiki.pulsedmedia.com/wiki/Computer_resource):

  • "A free 30-day trial (50 GiB, 250 MB RAM) is offered when trial slots are open" + 14-day money-back on paid plans. Slot availability is conditional — no guarantee a slot is open today.
  • User access (same page): "SSH — User-level shell access (no root). Run commands, manage files, install user-space software" + web panel with a browser shell console. Free tier is listed on the wiki as "Free Seedbox — full PMSS feature set, evaluation use."
  • Stack (wiki Seedbox page, fetched): torrent clients rTorrent/ruTorrent, Deluge, qBittorrent; file access SSH, SFTP, SCP, FTP, HTTPS downloads, WebDAV; 100+ pre-installed CLI tools incl. Python 3, p7zip/unrar, rclone; rootless Docker on all plans; public trackers allowed.
  • Limits that bite: the media-stack installer "stops on accounts with less than 1000 MiB of memory, so it does not fit the free trial (250 MB)" — irrelevant to torrenting, but it shows how thin the trial slice is.
  • Free page (fetched https://pulsedmedia.com/free-seedbox.php): "You may go beyond your storage limit by 25% for up to 7 days" — even bursting, 50 GiB → 62.5 GiB (~67 GB), still <125 GB and ≪350 GB.

docs.title: The shell / piece-priority path — why it still fails
docs.text:
Pulsed is the one candidate where the (b) path is technically real:

  • SSH + Python/libtorrent (or a custom client) can set piece priorities so only pieces overlapping the wanted zip ranges download, stored as a sparse file — qBittorrent's own UI/API only exposes file priorities, which are useless inside a single-file torrent.
  • But the wanted ranges total ~125 GB and the quota is 50 GiB (53.7 GB). Holding the wanted pieces at once overflows quota by ~2.3×; holding the full file overflows by ~6.5×. Quota enforcement would stall/kill the download long before completion.
  • The only theoretical workaround is a rotating batch loop: fetch a <50 GiB batch of pieces → extract those zip entries locally on the box (p7zip is pre-installed) → offload via SFTP/rclone/HTTPS → delete → repeat. That is unproven custom tooling on a 250 MB RAM trial account, dependent on an open trial slot, with zip central-directory handling and quota behaviour untested. It is a research project, not a backup path — especially when the TorBox direct path already works today.
  • HTTPS Range: files are served by per-user lighttpd over HTTPS, which in principle supports Range requests, but Pulsed does not document a Range guarantee — UNVERIFIED. SFTP (resumable) is documented and would be the reliable pull method.

docs.title: 3. Any other free-trial seedbox ≥100 GB?
docs.text:
None found. Web searches this session (queries on free-trial seedbox storage/SSH, Seedhost/Pulsed/Ultra specifically) surfaced only:

  • Ultra.cc — explicitly no trials. Official docs FAQ (via search): "Does Ultra.cc Offer Trials? No. Ultra.cc does not offer free trials" — new customers only get a 7-day first-order refund policy. Paid entry €4.95/mo / 1 TB would fit, but it is not free.
  • Pulsed comparison table (fetched): Whatbox, Feral Hosting, Seedboxes.cc, RapidSeedbox, Seedhost.eu, Ultra.cc — Free Tier: No for every one; Pulsed is the only "Yes" in the table.
  • Seedbox.io: money-back (14 days) only, no free trial found.
  • sdbx.moe ToS (via search): "A free 2 day trial is available … The request must be made on our Discord server" — 2 days, request-by-Discord (manual step), storage not published, no evidence of ≥100 GB, let alone 350 GB. Fails both the size-evidence and the no-manual-work tests.

No provider anywhere in the sweep offers a free trial with ≥100 GB storage. The largest verified free seedbox storage in existence here is Pulsed's 50 GiB.

docs.title: 4. Signup path (for completeness — NOT recommended)
docs.text:
Best candidate on paper is Pulsed (only real free trial + shell), and even it is dead on storage (above). If the parent ever wanted to confirm a slot anyway, it is browser-dependent — flagging clearly: this subagent cannot operate a live browser, and the parent's browser lane is noted as flaky.

  1. Browser → https://pulsedmedia.com/free-seedbox.php → order the free 30-day trial (WHMCS-style email signup; no Google OAuth advertised — Google sign-in fmmg.mars@gmail.com does not appear to be an option).
  2. If no slot is open, the flow dead-ends — availability is the first gate.
  3. Credentials arrive by email; SSH/SFTP details are in that email.
  4. Even with an account in hand: do NOT add the 350 GB magnet expecting selective download — see §2 math. The account cannot hold the result.

Seedhost "trial" path would be: browser → seedhost.eu → order HD 2 (€5, payment method required) → cancel within 7 days for refund. That is a purchase + refund gamble, requires payment details the owner has not offered for this, and is out of scope for a free-trial lane.

docs.title: Honest math summary
docs.text:
• Full file: 350,016,069,428 B = 326 GiB. Best free trial: 50 GiB. Shortfall 276 GiB (6.5×).
  • Wanted gaps only, all at once: ~125 GB ≈ 116 GiB vs 50 GiB. Shortfall ~66 GiB (2.3×); vs 62.5 GiB burst limit, still ~1.9× short.
  • Seedhost: free trial storage = does not exist in 2026 (paid + 7-day refund only).

Angle declared DEAD for this torrent. Keep the working TorBox direct path as primary; the only seedbox that would fit is a paid one (Seedhost HD 2 €5/mo / 2 TB + SSH, Ultra.cc €4.95/mo / 1 TB, Pulsed paid ≥1 TB tiers) — a purchase decision for the owner, not a free trial.

  • Seedhost shared plans + SSH FAQ (HD 1 1 TB €3 no SSH; HD 2 2 TB €5): https://www.seedhost.eu/shared-app-hosting/

docs.title: PRODUCERBOT WORKFLOW
docs.text: Canonical copy: mhvnsnt/western-heart docs/agent-handoff/PRODUCERBOT_WORKFLOW.md. Western Heart paths below refer to that repo.

docs.title: Producerbot workflow: how to continue exactly as Producerbot works
docs.text: Written 2026-10-14 so Muse and every other agent can pick up the owner's (mhvnsnt) work with no guessing. Repo-specific notes are at the bottom. When something here conflicts with an owner message, the owner wins: write the new rule here in the same PR.

docs.title: 0. Start of every task
docs.text:
1. Read this file, AGENTS.md, CANON.md (games), and the agent-ops board: mhvnsnt/agent-ops → TAG-TEAM.md (who is on what) and CLAIMS.md.
  2. Claim first. Add one line to CLAIMS.md (<agent> | <repo> | <task> | <date>) on a branch and open a PR with gh. Don't start work someone else claimed. Current owners: creation suite + teardown importers = Repo Co Dev; physics + physics test env = the physics agent; T-pose renders = Muse.
  3. Pull main before you touch shared files (git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main). Another job may be editing the same folder: work only in your files, resolve conflicts by keeping both sides.

docs.title: 1. Clones and disk (box is shared and often near full)
docs.text:
df -h /                                                     # check first; stop if < 3 GB free
git clone --filter=blob:none --depth 1 https://github.com/mhvnsnt/<repo> <dir>      # shallow, blobless
git clone --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/mhvnsnt/<repo> <dir> && cd <dir> && git sparse-checkout set <paths...>
- Clone into /workspace/<task>/, not into another agent's folder. - Back up before delete. Never delete anything that is not verified saved. For a clone: git status --porcelain | wc -l must be 0, git log --branches --not --remotes --oneline | wc -l must be 0, and every branch must show in git ls-remote origin. Stashes → push as backup/box-<date>-<name> branches. Uncommitted → commit to a backup/... branch, never main. - Big untracked/ignored files → private mhvnsnt/box-storage as Release assets: sha256sum f > f.sha256; gh release upload <tag> f f.sha256 -R mhvnsnt/box-storage, then download it back and compare SHA-256 before deleting the local copy. - Log every move with links in agent-ops BOX-OFFLOAD-LOG.md. Keep anything an agent is using right now. - Ports: 8765 and 8791 are often taken by others. Pick a high free port (python3 -m http.server 18437 -b 127.0.0.1 -d game).

docs.title: 2. Git, PRs, merging
docs.text:
• PRs only through the gh CLI from the box, never the connector "create PR" form (the owner refuses to submit forms): git push -u origin <branch> && gh pr create -R mhvnsnt/<repo> --head <branch> --title "..." --body "..."
  • Branch names grok/<repo-short>-<topic>. Small PRs, one piece each. Push each piece as soon as it's done (incremental pushes), never sit on local work.
  • Merge rule (owner, Oct 14 2026): a PR merges into main only if it merges cleanly, its tests/CI pass, and it deletes or breaks nothing on main. Otherwise it stays open. Repos with .github/workflows/pr-clean-merge.yml (money-machine-hq, God Molecule, TRIPPEDD, Bannon) auto-merge when green; it fails any PR that deletes a file on main, and it never auto-merges PRs touching .github/workflows (owner merges those).
  • Check before merging: gh pr checks <n> -R mhvnsnt/<repo> and gh pr view <n> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus. If checks are invisible or failing on main too, say so and leave the PR open.
  • Commit identity on the box: git config user.name "Producerbot (Grok Bot)"; git config user.email mhvnsnt@users.noreply.github.com.

docs.title: 3. Media proof standard (never claim without proof)
docs.text: Full gate list: /home/box/agent-data/workflows/media-proof-standard/SKILL.md. Short form: - Reopen the bytes you wrote (PIL verify, ffprobe, full ffmpeg -f null decode, GLB load). - Open the frames/PNGs yourself with an image reader and look: subject present, no blank frames, text spelled right. - SHA-256 every deliverable (sha256sum) into a manifest (parts.json / SHA256SUMS / PROVENANCE.md). - Edits to owner art/models: before/after of the same frame, side by side. - No AI faces. Characters are rendered from the owner's own models or real imports. AI only for non-character plates, labelled AI_PLATE. - Unknown origin = "parts unknown". Never invent canon. Card text comes from CANON.md through a script. - Version, never overwrite: _v2, _a1wip, base_v1. Originals and teardown files are never edited. - Never say "rescanned" for a recolor. Say what was actually done. - You can't hear audio: say so and ask the owner to listen.

docs.title: 4. How the Western Heart UI screens were built (game/ui-wh/, PR #121, #123)
docs.text:
1. Layouts mapped from teardowns, rebuilt not copied: title = TTT2/T6; main menu = Urban Reign/TTT2 list with JP sub-label; mode select = Def Jam/WWE cards; character select = T6/TTT2 (P1 left, P2 right, grid middle, timer); VS = Def Jam/WWE diagonal; HUD = T6 bars + Nine-Soul meter; pause = Urban Reign/Tekken; results = WWE/Def Jam. Table in game/ui-wh/README.md.
  2. Wallpaper transform: python3 game/ui-wh/tools/make_wallpaper.py derives art/wallpaper_wh.png from the owner's game/assets/ui/title-bg.png: 16:9 crop dropping the logo band → heavy blur (source characters become light) → indigo/crimson/gold duotone + crimson sun → Pantera rendered from his GLB as hero → Western Heart Japanese text. Source file untouched.
  3. Portraits from GLBs in Godot (no AI): xvfb-run -a godot --rendering-driver opengl3 --path lab/game -s res://tools/render_ui_portraits.gd -- $(pwd)/game/ui-wh/portraits. Any GLB + recipe: lab/game/tools/render_card.gd (see §5).
  4. Playwright capture + self-review loop: serve game/, then PW_CHROMIUM=/usr/bin/google-chrome WH_PORT=<port> node game/ui-wh/tools/capture.mjs docs/qa/ui-wh (needs a playwright install; on the box ln -s /tmp/gb-pw/node_modules node_modules temporarily, remove before commit). It fails on any page error / 404 / wrong active screen / broken keyboard flow. Then open every PNG, fix what looks wrong, capture again. Repeat until it passes AND looks right.

docs.title: 5. Roster cards and showcases (docs/roster/ROSTER_CARDS.md, PR #125)
docs.text:
python3 game/ui-wh/tools/canon_to_roster.py          # CANON.md -> game/ui-wh/roster_canon.json (never hand-edit)
# real render only if a model fits the canon description; else MODEL PENDING silhouette + full canon text
xvfb-run -a godot --rendering-driver opengl3 --path lab/game -s res://tools/render_card.gd -- $PWD/<glb> /tmp/<id> $PWD/docs/roster/<id>/kitbash_v1.json 20
WH_PORT=<port> PW_CHROMIUM=/usr/bin/google-chrome node game/ui-wh/tools/capture_cards.mjs docs/qa/roster-cards
- Lock state is data: roster.js isUnlocked(); Pantera only by default; ?unlock=all only for promo captures. - Card = render, name, kanji, soul, tier line, quote, Tekken body, element, ORIGIN parts unknown, signature. Flag on the art: ATTIRE 1 / WIP KITBASH / MODEL PENDING. - Kitbash (owner t48u): re-dress existing models with parts from every teardown (TTT2/T6, Def Jam, Urban Reign, WWE) on versioned copies; log every part in docs/roster/<id>/parts.json with source, SHA-256, third_party, pre-sale action. Worked example: docs/roster/zui/ (base T7 Steve Fox import → hide hair, robe recolour, indigo pants, sake gourd, beads, sash → before/after + SHA-256). Honest gap: no extracted head/hair meshes from TTT2/Def Jam/Urban Reign/WWE are on main yet. - Showcase = select (default + unlock all) + every card + promo strip (cards.html#strip?ids=...). Look at every PNG before reporting.

docs.title: 6. Height / scale system (PR #120)
docs.text: lab/game/data/characters/heights.json (cm per fighter) → lab/game/scripts/height_scale.gd scales each fighter at fight load; HUD shows height; tests lab/game/tests/test_height_scale.gd (46 pass). Tekken 6/TTT2 publish no heights; values borrowed from Tekken 7/8 profiles need owner OK (rule check holds it).

docs.title: 7. T-pose and model co-author pipeline
docs.text: T-pose standard: docs/tpose-refs/MUSE_TPOSE_SPEC.md (one-to-one T-pose, pure white, fingertips in frame, flat light, every attire). Flow: T-pose image → Tripo 3D → rig (Tripo/Mixamo) → python3 tools/import_model.py <glb> --character <id> --attire <a> --render (rig map, Tekken segments, P1 retarget map, rig gates, register; docs/MODEL_IMPORT_AUTORIG.md) → co-author in Blender / creation suite (docs/CREATE_A_FIGHTER_SPEC.md, Repo Co Dev) → move-set (docs/MOVESET_EDITOR_SPEC.md). Drive links: AGENT_IMPORT_RUNBOOK in CREATE_A_FIGHTER_SPEC.md. Secondary/jiggle bone names for the physics sandbox: MODEL_IMPORT_AUTORIG.md.

docs.title: 8. Entrance videos
docs.text: Exact method: money-machine-hq/docs/production-bible/ENTRANCE_VIDEO_METHOD.md (also in Bannon, God Molecule, TRIPPEDD): rig repair, animation, ring + lights, name plate and cards, beat-grid edit (every cut on the beat grid), music, post commands, vertical cut. Owner's spelling rules apply (e.g. "STICK UP", no hyphen).

docs.title: 9. Teardown → proprietary rule
docs.text: Build on top, never destroy. Teardown files stay byte-identical; everything new is a derived, versioned file. Transform into the Eastern Mind · Western Heart universe (names, souls, kanji, colours, parts) until it reads as ours. Track every remaining third-party piece (third_party: true + pre-sale action in parts.json / move slots) so it can be replaced before any sale. Tell the owner plainly what is still third-party.

docs.title: 10. Honesty rules
docs.text:
• Report failures, blocks and gaps in the same message as the wins.
  • Never say done, fixed, merged or "looks better" without the proof from §3 and a link.
  • Never claim to have watched/listened. Never invent canon, faces or data.
  • Prefer a smaller true result over a bigger claimed one.
